events.text: Nobody in the Cult would dare ask you who comes next. They ask each other. This spring the Hall Masters' servants carry two sets of gifts up the black steps, one to {ot_child} and one to {ot_foe}, and both are heavier than a gift should be. You have named nobody, and on this mountain an empty place on the steps does not stay empty for long.

choices.text: Have them both stand beside you at the drums

effects.log: They stand one on each side of you and do not look at each other. Everyone counts the paces between you and each of them.

choices.text: Say nothing. Strength is law

effects.log: You say nothing. By summer it is understood that the Heavenly Demon wishes to see who is stronger, whether you do or not.

events.text: {ot_child} has started taking breakfast with the Black Drum Hall. {ot_foe} has taken to walking the Hall of Tallies in the evening, asking about grain. Neither has said a word against the other. In a place where people are thrown from cliffs for less, their manners have become very good, and it is the good manners that wake you in the night.

choices.text: Send each of them away on the same day, in opposite directions

effects.log: Each comes back a year later with friends they did not have before. You have at least had a quiet year.

choices.text: Ask {ot_child} what the Black Drum Hall serves at breakfast

effects.log: {ot_He} tells you, smiling, down to the pickles. {ot_He} has understood that you know. {ot_He} has understood that you did not stop it.

events.text: {ot_child} wants nothing from this mountain but to be left with {ot_his} own arts. It has not helped. A Hall Master has sent a name-tablet to {ot_his} door, with {ot_his} name already carved and a place left for a date. If {ot_he} does not stand, {ot_foe} stands alone, and nobody on these steps has ever been allowed to stand aside from someone standing alone.

choices.text: Tell {ot_child} {ot_he} may refuse

effects.log: {ot_He} thanks you and asks how. You find you do not have an answer. {ot_He} keeps the tablet, face down.

choices.text: Tell {ot_him} to stand up straight, then

effects.log: {ot_He} looks at you for some time. Then {ot_he} stands up straight, and it is a long time before you see {ot_him} laugh again.

events.text: At the Festival of the Black Drum both of your heirs ask to beat the first stroke. It is a very small honour. By nightfall every hall has an opinion, the kitchens have taken sides, and two guards of no importance have broken each other's noses over {ot_child}'s drumming.

choices.text: Beat the first stroke yourself

effects.log: You have not beaten it in twenty years, and your arm remembers. Nobody can say whom you were snubbing, so everyone says it was them.

choices.text: Give it to {ot_child}

effects.log: {ot_child} beats it very well. {ot_foe} applauds with the rest and has the drum's skin quietly examined afterwards.

events.text: {ot_foe} has beaten an orthodox master on the border, and rides home with the man's banner across {ot_fhis} saddle. Within the month {ot_child} is on the road with forty riders, looking for a bigger banner. The murim has begun to notice that the Cult's raids are getting very frequent and very well reported.

choices.text: Forbid raids without your seal

effects.log: They both obey at once. The raids stop being reported.

choices.text: Keep the banners. Hang them in the hall

effects.log: The hall looks splendid. It is now a scoreboard, and you have told them so.

events.text: {ot_child} sits in the lower hall with the young captains and lets them talk. {ot_He} never promises anything. {ot_He} remembers the names of their mothers. {ot_foe} calls it begging and trains alone on the black cliff where everyone can see {ot_fhim}. You watched each of your own teachers lose to one of those two kinds of person, and you cannot remember which kind you were.

choices.text: Take {ot_foe} to the lower hall and make {ot_fhim} sit

effects.log: {ot_foe} sits, badly, for an hour. A captain laughs at something {ot_fhe} says, and {ot_fhe} is so surprised that it nearly becomes a habit.

choices.text: Train on the cliff beside {ot_foe} at dawn

effects.log: The whole Cult sees it by noon. {ot_child} sends you a very polite note about the weather on the cliff.

events.text: A Hall of Tallies clerk is caught with a second set of books. The second set shows that {ot_child} has been paying for the swords of three squads out of the Cult's own silver. It is beautifully kept, and the hand is just slightly too neat. You have known real embezzlers, and they are never this tidy. {ot_foe} has come to tell you how much the news grieves {ot_fhim}.

choices.text: Read the books yourself, line by line

ok.log: The ink on the first year and the last is the same batch. You send the books to {ot_foe} with that page marked, and no note.

fail.log: It could be true. It could be anything. You hate how much this looks like everything you have been told about your own rise.

choices.text: Punish {ot_child} for being careless enough to be framed

effects.log: You have the three squads moved. On this mountain it is the only lesson there is, and {ot_child} understands it, and does not forgive it.

events.text: Someone has been paying your people to lose things. A shipment of {ot_foe}'s pills has fallen in a river. A letter of {ot_child}'s has been read aloud in a tavern, in a very good imitation of {ot_his} voice. Your own steward has come into a small house in the valley, and is hoping you do not ask about it.

choices.text: Ask about the small house

effects.log: He weeps and tells you everything he knows, which is that the silver was new. You keep him on. A frightened steward is worth two loyal ones.

choices.text: Let it be known the next one to take silver goes off the cliff

effects.log: It stops for a whole season. Then the price of everything in the Cult goes up, because now there is a risk to pay for.

events.text: A letter turns up in {ot_foe}'s rooms, in {ot_child}'s hand, promising a place to a Sect Leader of the orthodox side. For anyone else in the Cult it would be a death sentence. It has been found by exactly the right guard, on exactly the right morning, and half the Hall Masters already know what it says.

choices.text: Burn it in front of them, unread

effects.log: They watch it burn. {ot_child} bows to you. Nobody will ever know now whether it was true, and that includes you.

choices.text: Have it read aloud, and watch both faces

effects.log: One face goes white, and the other has been practising. You still could not swear which is which.

events.text: {ot_child} comes to the morning drums with a bandaged hand and an easy smile. A needle was left in the grip of {ot_his} training sword. It would have been a bad week for anyone else, but {ot_he} has been expecting it for a year. {ot_foe} sends a very good physician, at once, and {ot_child} sends the physician back with a very good gift.

choices.text: Have the armoury's keepers put to the question

effects.log: They tell you who paid. It is someone who was paid by someone. By the third name the trail has gone cold on purpose.

choices.text: Move {ot_child}'s rooms next to yours

effects.log: It stops the needles. It also tells the whole mountain who you would rather keep alive.

events.text: Three men came over the wall of {ot_foe}'s hall last night, in the colours of a sect that has not been seen this side of the mountains in decades. {ot_foe} fought them in {ot_fhis} sleeping clothes and has a long cut on the arm to show for it. In the morning all three have somehow died in the cells, before anyone could ask them anything.

choices.text: Find out who holds the keys to the cells

effects.log: {ot_child}'s man held them, or a man who looks like {ot_child}'s man. You have him sent to the far gate, and let everyone wonder why.

choices.text: Tell them both, in one room, that you know

effects.log: You do not know, but they do not know that. It goes quiet, for about as long as it takes them to work it out.

events.text: It starts over a door. A squad of {ot_child}'s will not give way to a squad of {ot_foe}'s in the covered walk of the Black Drum Hall, and by the time you get there it has reached the second courtyard. Forty people are fighting under your roof, and the Cult's own art is being used on the Cult's own stairs.

choices.text: Walk in between them, alone, and stand there

ok.log: It stops, one row at a time, from the front to the back. Nobody wants to be the last one with a raised hand. You stand there until sunset to make the point.

fail.log: It stops when your palm has put eleven of them through a wall. It should have stopped when you walked in. Everyone noticed that it did not.

choices.text: Let it burn out, and count who is still standing

effects.log: You watch from the upper gallery. It is a useful count. It costs you two good captains, and everyone knows you watched.

events.text: The drums are beating at the wrong hour. {ot_foe}'s people have taken the Hall of Tallies, to protect it, they say, from {ot_child}'s people, who have taken the upper granary, to protect that. The servants have started carrying their bedding down the mountain. It has not been this loud here since you were the one taking halls.

choices.text: Order both sides off the halls before the drums stop

effects.log: They go, slowly, with their hands near their swords, and each leaves one person behind by accident. The mountain breathes out, a little.

choices.text: Send your own guard to hold the granary for {ot_foe}

effects.log: It is over by morning, in that hall at least. You have now done with your hand what you would not do with your mouth.

events.text: The Hall Masters have asked to see you, all of them, together. Nobody has done that since your own coronation. They kneel on the black stone and the oldest of them says it plainly: this ends this year, one way or another. {ot_child} has the most of it. {ot_foe} is close behind. The mountain cannot be held by a silence any longer.

choices.text: Name {ot_child}, before the whole Cult

effects.log: You set your hand on {ot_his} head. It is done. You hear the drums start up, and you try not to listen for who is not beating them.

choices.text: Break {ot_foe}, so that there is nothing left to choose

effects.log: It takes an afternoon. {ot_foe} kneels when it is over, and looks at you, and you will see that look again.

choices.text: Say nothing again, and let the Cult split

effects.log: They bow and go. In a month {ot_foe} goes too, down the western road, with a third of the banners. It is what you chose, and you did it without a word.

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} has walked up to {ot_child}'s rooms in the middle of the day, by the main stair, and stayed for tea. On this mountain that is a speech. {He} says {ot_child} understands what the hall wants, which is {ot_want}. {ot_foe} has already sent to ask what it would take to change {his} mind.

choices.text: Let it stand

effects.log: It stands. The whole mountain now knows where one more hall is. That at least makes it easier to count.

choices.text: Send {npc} a gift that says you noticed

effects.log: {He} reads the gift very well, and finds that {he} has been misunderstood about the tea. {He} is nobody's for the moment. (-300 taels)

events.text: Your ears in {ot_hall} tell you the lamp-oil has got better. So have the new boots of {npc}'s captains. The silver is coming down by way of two merchants and a dead uncle, and it starts in {ot_child}'s accounts. {npc} has not said anything to anyone, and will go on being very correct to everybody, until the day it matters.

choices.text: Outbid {ot_child}, quietly

effects.log: It costs less than you feared. It tells you more than you wanted about what your halls cost. (-400 taels)

choices.text: Leave it, and let {npc} learn you know

effects.log: A very small note reaches {him}: the price of the boots, to the copper. {He} goes on being correct, a little more carefully.

events.text: There will be a wedding on the black steps. {npc} of {ot_hall} is giving a niece, a hall's worth of swords comes with the match, and {ot_child} has said yes without asking you. Everyone agrees that it is a very suitable match. {ot_foe} has sent a magnificent gift, and has also started looking at who {ot_fhe} might marry.

choices.text: Bless the match in front of them all

effects.log: You bless it. It is a good feast. You raise a cup of tea to the match, and it is hard to say which of you is using which.

choices.text: Find the niece a better match, somewhere far away

effects.log: A prince of the far west asks for the niece, very suddenly, with a lot of money you provided. {npc} knows. {He} will not say so, ever. (-500 taels)

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} used to dine with {ot_foe}. Your listeners tell you that for the last three months {he} has dined with {ot_foe} and then sent a boy up the back way to {ot_child}, with what was said. {ot_foe} still thinks that hall is {ot_fhis}. It is a very elegant piece of work, and you are a little sorry not to have thought of it.

choices.text: Say nothing. It is useful to know

effects.log: You say nothing. Now you know one more thing than both of them, which is the only real rank on this mountain.

choices.text: See to it that {ot_foe} finds out

effects.log: One overheard remark is all it takes. {ot_foe} does not shout. {ot_fHe} sends {npc} a very fine knife, in a box, with a thank-you note.

events.text: They found {npc} of {ot_hall} at the bottom of the Long Stair this morning. It was a fall, the physician says, without looking up. {He} had been {ot_child}'s for a year, and had climbed that stair every day for forty. There will be a new {ot_title} by the end of the mourning, and {ot_foe} has already sent flowers to the widow.

choices.text: Say out loud what everyone is thinking

effects.log: You say it at the funeral, over the body, with the name. It does nothing for {npc}. It does a good deal to {ot_foe}, for a while.

choices.text: Bury {him} well and say nothing

effects.log: It is a very good funeral. Everyone takes note of what can be done on your stairs and be called a fall.

events.text: {npc} of the Black Drum Hall comes up the steps as if inspecting them. {He} wants a war worth beating the drums for. {He} has been drilling the same ten thousand men for nine years against nobody, and says plainly that whichever of your heirs gives {him} a war will have {him}. Unless you do it first.

choices.text: Go and look at the drills, and tell {him} where the drills are wrong

ok.log: {He} stares at you, and then stays until dark over the maps. Nobody has talked to {him} like that in years. You have {him}, and you did not even have to start a war.

fail.log: {He} hears you out with great respect, and goes back down. You have told a soldier about soldiering.

choices.text: Promise {him} the next border fight, and mean it

effects.log: {He} kneels, and it is a real kneel. The price is on the calendar now, and {ot_child} will hear of it.

choices.text: Tell {him} to keep drilling

effects.log: {He} bows. You can hear {his} boots all the way down the stair.

events.text: {npc} of the Hall of Shut Doors comes in by a door you had forgotten. {He} wants to be told things first, and what {he} is really asking is who you mean to name. {He} says that for one word, whispered, {he} would make sure nobody else ever heard a thing. {He} has been making that offer to people for a very long time, and is mostly still alive.

choices.text: Tell {him} something true, that nobody else knows

effects.log: It costs you a secret you have kept since the throne. {He} closes {his} eyes as if tasting it. The hall is yours, until someone has a better one.

choices.text: Tell {him} something false, and see where it comes back from

effects.log: It comes back in four days, from {ot_child}'s side of the mountain. Now you know where that door opens.

choices.text: Show {him} out by the main stair, where everyone can see

effects.log: Everyone sees. {He} does not look annoyed. {He} looks as though {he} has written something down.

events.text: {npc} of the Hall of Tallies has brought two ledgers and an apology for the second. {He} wants silver, and an end to questions about silver. {He} is quite open about it. {He} says all your heirs have made offers, that your offer would naturally carry the most weight, and that it would have to be more than theirs.

choices.text: Pay what {he} asks

effects.log: {He} counts it twice, in front of you, without embarrassment. From now on the books of the Cult will say whatever you need. (-800 taels)

choices.text: Read the second ledger, and ask about page nine

ok.log: There is a long pause. {He} closes the book and says that {he} has always admired you. Page nine is yours to keep, and so is {he}.

fail.log: Page nine turns out to be perfectly in order. {He} does not smile, which is kind of {him}.

choices.text: Send {him} away with both ledgers

effects.log: {He} goes. The Cult's silver goes on being counted by someone you have just told you can do without.

events.text: {npc} of the Cold Furnace Hall has not left it in eleven years, and comes up the steps blinking. {He} wants the old arts kept as they were, and nobody to hurry them. Your heirs both keep sending young people to learn the fast forms for the fighting to come. {He} has sent all of them home, and is here to ask if you mean to send {him} home as well.

choices.text: Sit with {him} at the furnace and do the old form slowly, all of it

ok.log: It takes three days. Your hands remember less than you thought. At the end {he} corrects your wrist, which nobody has dared to do since you were young. {He} is yours.

fail.log: You lose the thread on the second day. {He} is too polite to say so, and shows you out.

choices.text: Give your word nobody will be sent to {him} but by your hand

effects.log: {He} thinks about it for some time, and nods. It is a small thing, and both of your heirs have just lost something by it.

choices.text: Tell {him} the fighting will not wait for a furnace

effects.log: {He} nods, as one who has heard that before, from people whose names are on the wall. {He} goes back to it.

events.text: {ot_child} has stopped coming to the morning drums. You named {ot_foe}, and the whole Cult bowed, and {ot_child} bowed too, last of all, and lower than anyone. Since then {ot_his} people have started to take the long way round through the halls. One of them has been seen at the western gate, counting the guards, for no reason at all.

choices.text: Go to {ot_his} rooms and ask {ot_him} what {ot_he} wants instead

effects.log: It takes the whole night, and {ot_he} shouts, which {ot_he} has never done. In the morning {ot_he} asks for the frontier command. It is a good answer. You give it to {ot_him}.

choices.text: Send {ot_him} down the mountain before it starts

effects.log: {ot_He} goes with a very straight back. {ot_foe} sleeps better, and the western road has something new to talk about.

choices.text: Leave it. Let the named one deal with it

effects.log: If {ot_fhe} cannot hold this, {ot_fhe} cannot hold the mountain. It is a good argument, and it is also what you would say if you were afraid.

events.text: They have carried the old throne's cloth out to be washed. Your parent named nobody. On the morning after the burning, {ot_foe} walks to the foot of the black steps and stands there, not climbing, with half of the Hall Masters a pace behind. You are standing at the other side of the courtyard. The whole of the Cult is on the walls, and it is waiting to see who moves.

choices.text: Walk to the steps and stand on the first one

effects.log: You take the first step, and no higher. Nobody strikes you. It is your claim, and now they all know it.

choices.text: Send to {ot_foe} and offer to talk

effects.log: {ot_fHe} sends back that {ot_fhe} will be glad to talk from the top. It costs you a little, in front of everyone. It may be worth having asked.

events.text: The Hall Masters will come to whoever can make them believe, and the houses will come to whoever is winning. You have until the thaw. You can spend it on the walls, among the squads, eating what they eat. Or you can spend it in the Hall of Tallies, buying everything that can be bought before {ot_foe} does.

choices.text: Go and eat with the squads

effects.log: By the thaw there are men in the lower hall who would tell you that they have always been yours. A few of them even have.

choices.text: Buy the Hall of Tallies out from under {ot_foe}

effects.log: The silver goes up the stairs at night. {ot_foe}'s pay-chests arrive in spring and are lighter than expected. (-600 taels)

choices.text: Train. It will come to that

effects.log: You train until your hands bleed. Everyone hears about it. Nobody comes over to you because of it, and you get a little stronger.

events.text: The fighting reaches the great halls at last. {ot_foe}'s people hold the upper stair, and your people want it. There is no one left to tell either side to stop. You could send someone else up those steps, or go first yourself, where every hall on the mountain can see your back.

choices.text: Go up first

ok.log: You go up first and they follow. By nightfall the upper stair is yours, and it has a new story, and you are in it.

fail.log: They hold. You come back down, on your feet, with fewer people than went up. The story has got round before you have got your breath.

choices.text: Let your captains take it, and hold the rest

effects.log: They take it, slowly, at a price. You have lost some standing with people who wanted to see you do it. You still have the people.

events.text: There is only the black stone now, and the two of you, and the whole Cult on the walls. {ot_foe} sets {ot_fhis} coat down carefully. In this house the throne goes to whoever walks away from this. If you lose, it is {ot_foe}'s, and whatever you have held goes with it, and there will be no appeal to anybody. Even now you could speak, or kneel.

choices.text: Fight

ok.log: It takes longer than either of you thought. {ot_foe} goes down at last and does not rise, and the drums begin before you have got your breath.

fail.log: You are looking up at the sky, and then at {ot_foe}, who is looking down. {ot_fHe} does not finish it. The drums begin, for someone else.

choices.text: Offer {ot_foe} the Black Drum Hall, and all the honour of it, to step down

ok.log: It takes all day, and you do not know what it is that finally does it. {ot_fHe} steps down. You did not win, exactly, and nobody will ever call it that. The throne is yours.

fail.log: {ot_fHe} hears you out. Then {ot_fhe} says that you have just told everyone you are afraid. It will be the stone after all, next year, and you have lost some ground.

choices.text: Kneel, first and in front of everyone

effects.log: You kneel. The sound the Cult makes is not quite a sigh. It is over, and you are alive, and that is all it is.

events.text: {ot_foe} is alive, and on {ot_fhis} knees at the foot of the steps, and waiting. The Cult's law on this is very old and quite short. Nobody expects mercy. A good many expect a show. There is a person there you once shared a room with, and they are watching what you do to find out what you are.

choices.text: Spare {ot_foe}, and give {ot_fhim} a hall to run

effects.log: It is talked about for years, mostly as a mistake. {ot_foe} bows, and goes to the hall, and it will be a long time before you know what you bought.

choices.text: Send {ot_fhim} down the western road

effects.log: {ot_fHe} goes with one bag. You do not watch from the wall. You stay away from the wall for some time.

choices.text: The old law, then

effects.log: It is quick. The Cult bows its ten thousand heads. You do not sleep well that year, or the next, and nobody ever again mentions {ot_foe}'s name in front of you.

events.text: {ot_foe} sits the throne now, and has sent for you. The black steps are a long way to walk with everyone watching. {ot_fHe} has not decided anything, or is pretending not to have. It could go several ways, and you would still rather choose one of them than have it chosen.

choices.text: Kneel to {ot_foe}, first and lowest

effects.log: You kneel, and {ot_fhe} gives you a chair in the second row, and everyone can see it from the door. You are alive. Some mornings that is enough.

choices.text: Go down the goat path tonight

effects.log: You take one bag. The sentries on the path look carefully the other way, and you will never know who told them to.

events.text: You keep a hall of the Cult, and so two heirs of the one who sits above you have started to remember your birthday. {ot_child} sends a fine horse. {ot_foe} sends a finer sword, and a note saying the horse is lame. Each of them wants the same thing, which is to be able to say that your hall stands with them. They would like an answer by the drums.

choices.text: Thank {ot_child} for the horse, in public

effects.log: {ot_He} is very gracious. Your hall has a side now, and so do the people who have to work with it.

choices.text: Wear {ot_foe}'s sword to the drums

effects.log: {ot_foe} looks at it, and looks pleased, and says nothing. You are now somebody's.

choices.text: Send both gifts back, with thanks

effects.log: It is noticed. You are the only person on the mountain who has not been bought, and they both hate that about you.

events.text: The one above you has fallen ill, or is said to have. The drums have been beating at odd hours, and your heir of choice has sent for your hall tonight. You know the way this goes on this mountain. People who come when called do very well, or do not come back, and either way it gets written down.

choices.text: Bring every sword you have

effects.log: You go in full armour, with drums, at the head of everyone. Nobody can say afterwards that you hedged.

choices.text: Bring half, and leave the rest with the gate

effects.log: It is a soldier's answer. Whoever wins will notice, and it will not make you loved.

events.text: The Blood Altar keeps a book of who is owed what, and it is older than the mountains' names for themselves. This year someone has opened it at the page of the succession and left it open. There are two names in it in fresh ink, {ot_child} and {ot_foe}, with a line ruled under them. No hand has been seen. The Elders have read it, and they have begun to bring their own lamps.

choices.text: Close the book, and have the page washed

effects.log: It takes three days to wash a page in that book. The names can still be read. It is the first time anyone has dared to touch it, and everyone knows who did.

choices.text: Leave it open. Let the debt be counted

effects.log: Everything here is counted. You leave it open. By the next new moon each of them has a column.

events.text: On the red night, when the raids are tallied, it is the custom for the Blood God's heir to carry the last lamp. Nobody has ever needed telling who that is. Tonight the lamp stands on the altar, lit, with two sets of attendants a careful distance apart. {ot_child} looks at it, and {ot_foe} looks at it, and then they both look at you.

choices.text: Carry it yourself, as if that were the rite

effects.log: You take it. Nobody breathes. The oldest Elder writes something down, and you cannot read it from here.

choices.text: Have it put out. There will be no last lamp this year

effects.log: It goes out with a very small sound. That is the first time in four hundred years, and they will be counting from it.

events.text: {ot_child} keeps the Altar's accounts and likes it. {ot_He} has no wish to be anything else. But the Left Lamp has brought {ot_him} an old debt: {ot_his} own birth was entered as owed to the altar, and it may be called in. All {ot_he} needs to do to clear it is to stand against {ot_foe}, who is otherwise going to be standing alone. It is all in order. {ot_He} checked the sums.

choices.text: Strike the entry out in your own hand

effects.log: It is the kind of thing only the Blood God can do, and it is the kind of thing nobody forgets. {ot_child} looks at you as if you had spoken a foreign language.

choices.text: Say the book is the book

effects.log: {ot_child} nods. {ot_He} goes and gets {ot_his} coat. {ot_He} has always been so good with numbers.

events.text: It is the season of tithes. {ot_child}'s people have brought in more to the altar than {ot_foe}'s, and they have brought it in very publicly, on carts. {ot_foe} has answered by bringing in less, but older: a sealed jar from a sect the world believes vanished. The Elders are very moved. In the crimson robes they have started keeping a score, though only on their fingers.

choices.text: Declare the tithe closed, and the tally sealed

effects.log: Nobody is allowed to count this year. They all have it memorised by morning.

choices.text: Have both offerings displayed, with a clerk to read out the sums

effects.log: The clerk has a fine voice. By the fifth line nobody in the hall is looking at the altar.

events.text: {ot_foe} has been sitting up with the oldest Master of the Hall, learning to read the first ledger, in a script nobody has used since the first raid. {ot_child} has discovered that someone is teaching {ot_fhim}, and has discovered a sudden love of very old languages. It is a strange thing to see two grown people quarrel over a dead grammar, and to know what it is for.

choices.text: Have the old script taught to all the blood, openly

effects.log: It is taught, and it is dull. In a year nobody is interested. You have ruined a very good secret and possibly saved a life.

choices.text: Sit in on {ot_foe}'s lesson, once

effects.log: You sit at the back. The old Master does not look up. {ot_child} hears about it before you have got your robe off.

events.text: It is the custom of the Altar for those of the blood to fast before the red night. {ot_child} fasted nine days. {ot_foe} fasted ten, and walked to the altar unsupported. {ot_child} has now announced eleven, and {ot_his} physician has come to you privately, looking old. Nobody can stop it without seeming to doubt somebody's devotion.

choices.text: Declare the fast ended by your own word, for everyone

effects.log: They eat. Each of them looks at you as though you have robbed them, and they are both alive to do it.

choices.text: Say nothing, and send the physician back

effects.log: {ot_child} walks to the altar on the eleventh day. {ot_He} gets there. It takes some time, and {ot_foe} watches all of it, and nods.

events.text: An entry has appeared in the Hall of the Long Count that says {ot_child} owes the altar a life. It is properly witnessed, in a hand no one can quite place, and it dates from a raid {ot_he} truly was on. In this house that is not a rumour, it is a bill. {ot_foe} has mentioned how sorry {ot_fhe} would be to see it presented.

choices.text: Trace the ink and the witness marks

ok.log: The witness was dead by that date. You have it read out, once, and there is a very long silence, and {ot_foe} develops an interest in the far provinces.

fail.log: It is good work. It may even be true. You have no way to say it is not, and the bill stands.

choices.text: Pay it, and have the page marked settled

effects.log: You pay in silver, which is very nearly an insult. It is marked settled. {ot_child} owes you now instead, which {ot_he} also notes. (-500 taels)

events.text: The crimson robes of {ot_foe}'s squads have begun to run short of the good dye, because someone has bought all of it. It sounds like nothing. In the Blood Cult a robe gone brown is a shame you can see from the far end of the valley, and {ot_foe}'s people have begun to be laughed at in the corridors. Behind this the same someone has been hiring the laughers.

choices.text: Have the dye shared out from the Altar's own store

effects.log: It is very fair, and it costs {ot_child} a season's clever work. {ot_He} sends you a small bolt of perfect red, without a note.

choices.text: Let them laugh. Robes are for those who cannot win

effects.log: {ot_foe}'s squads go out brown, and come home with the best tally of the year. You have the feeling you have started something.

events.text: A listener comes to you with a thing that has been said in a very low voice: that the Blood God's arts are failing, and that this is why you have named nobody. It has been said in four halls this month, always by someone who then seems to have forgotten having said it. Whoever is doing this has been careful, and is good at it, and believes you are too old to do anything about it.

choices.text: Hold the red night's rites yourself, all of them, in full

effects.log: It takes everything you have, and you do it in front of everyone with your hands steady. The saying stops. You sleep for three days.

choices.text: Find the first mouth

effects.log: You find it. It leads to a very frightened clerk and from there to a gift, and the gift came from {ot_child}. You keep the clerk close, and you say nothing yet.

events.text: A cup was poured for {ot_foe} at the Altar, the cup you do not refuse. {ot_fHe} drank it. {ot_fHe} also spent the next nine days not dying, because the Blood Cult's heirs have been raising their tolerance since before they could walk. There is nothing left of the cup-bearer but a new vacancy. {ot_child} has come to pray for {ot_fhis} recovery, loudly, in the front row.

choices.text: Have every cup in the Altar broken, and start again

effects.log: It costs more than you would think. The new ones are very plain. Nobody can say you did nothing.

choices.text: Sit by {ot_foe}'s bed yourself, where {ot_child} can see

effects.log: You sit there four nights. {ot_foe} wakes on the fifth, and sees you, and {ot_fhe} says nothing about it, and neither does anyone else.

events.text: On the raid to the salt towns {ot_child}'s squad was left without its reserve for most of a night, because of an order nobody now remembers giving. {ot_He} brought back nine out of forty, and a wound that will not close well. {ot_foe} has been the first to send condolences for each of the thirty-one. {ot_fHe} has spelled their names correctly, every one.

choices.text: Find the order

effects.log: You find a copy. The hand is very like {ot_foe}'s, in the way that a very good copy is. You put it in the ledger, on the page where it can wait.

choices.text: Enter the thirty-one against {ot_foe}'s account, without proof

effects.log: You write it yourself. It is not justice, and nobody in the Blood Hall thinks it should be. They read it and understand what can be owed.

events.text: The two Halls have stopped sending each other their dead for the rites. Two sets of processions, in two reds, met on the stair below the Altar this evening, and neither gave way, and now the stair is being held. There are people here who have been waiting all their lives to find out which of the old arts really work on those who know them.

choices.text: Go down with the last lamp, lit, and say the old words

ok.log: It has not been done in living memory. They stop. Some of them weep, and none of them could tell you why. You have used something you may not be able to use twice.

fail.log: You say them, and half of them hear you. That half stop, and it is the wrong half. It goes on until dark.

choices.text: Close the Altar's doors and let the stair settle it

effects.log: You have the doors shut. You can hear it from inside. In the morning there is one kind of red on the stair, and a very great deal to enter in the book.

events.text: The Hall of the Long Count has been sealed from inside by {ot_child}'s people, with the whole of the ledgers in it. {ot_foe}'s people have the cisterns. Nobody in the Blood Cult can now say what they are owed or draw what they need. Somewhere below, the crimson robes have started asking one another what exactly the Blood God is for.

choices.text: Order the Hall opened in your name, by force

effects.log: You send your own guard. The doors come off. {ot_child} walks out with empty hands and looks at you, and the ledgers are all there, and all in order. It is very frightening.

choices.text: Pay out of your own vault, until they are ashamed

effects.log: You pay every squad, on the steps, in person, for a month. Nobody knows what to do with this. It goes quiet, out of something like embarrassment. (-700 taels)

events.text: Both Masters and both Elders have come to you with the book, and they lay it open at the page. It has been running for a long time now, and the two columns are close. They tell you, without any expression, that it is in the nature of a ledger to be closed. Who closes it is the only thing that has ever been left to the Blood God.

choices.text: Rule the line under {ot_child}'s name

effects.log: You rule it in your own hand. It is a very straight line. The lamps go up on one side of the hall, and on the other somebody starts to count something.

choices.text: Strike {ot_foe}'s column through

effects.log: Everything {ot_fhe} has earned here, gone, in one stroke. It is the most terrible thing that can be done with a pen in this house. {ot_fHe} watches you do it.

choices.text: Close the book unruled, and let it fall as it falls

effects.log: You shut it. In a month {ot_foe} has left for the salt country, with the older of the two reds and a copy of the book. Now there are two ledgers.

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} has entered {ot_child}'s name in {his} own day-book, in the column of those {he} serves, and left it where anyone can read it. {He} says {ot_child} has shown that {ot_he} understands what is needed, which is {ot_want}. It is not an oath, since those are for the young. It is merely an entry, and {he} has never yet altered an entry.

choices.text: Read it, and initial it, as one who keeps accounts

effects.log: You put your mark beside it. It is witnessed now, and everyone in the Hall can count one more on that side.

choices.text: Send {npc} a gift of old ink, and ask if {he} is sure

effects.log: {He} considers the ink for some time. Next morning that line has been ruled out, neatly, with a note that it was entered in error. (-300 taels)

events.text: There is a small hole in the Altar's accounts, and it is a very honest hole, the shape of what {npc} of {ot_hall} has been receiving. It comes from {ot_child}, by way of a salt merchant who owes {ot_him} a life. {npc} sees nothing wrong with this. {He} regards it as a tithe, offered to the right place.

choices.text: Enter a larger tithe in {his} name yourself

effects.log: {He} receives it with exactly the same expression. {He} has always said the altar provides. (-400 taels)

choices.text: Have the hole read out at the next tally

effects.log: The clerk reads it out. Nobody turns a head. {npc} corrects a figure. Now at least everyone knows what {he} costs.

events.text: There are old rules for a marriage into the Blood Altar, and they take a year, and {npc} of {ot_hall} has been observing them. {His} heir is to be joined to {ot_child}, the hands bound in a red cord, the debts of both lines entered as one. It is the first such joining in sixty years. Nobody has asked you, and the rules do not say that anyone has to.

choices.text: Bind the cord yourself

effects.log: You tie it, in the old knot. The line of {ot_hall} is on that side of the ledger now, under your own hand.

choices.text: Discover an old debt that bars the match

effects.log: It takes the Long Count a week to find one. It is real, too; there always is one. The cord goes back in its box, and {npc} looks at you without hurry. (-500 taels)

events.text: Your listener has compared two columns. For a year {npc} of {ot_hall} has been entering {his} service to {ot_foe} in the ordinary ink, and a second set of figures, in a thin brown ink, for {ot_child}. {ot_foe} has not yet thought to hold the page up to a lamp. You have to admit this is the most devout treachery you have ever seen.

choices.text: Hold your peace, and hold the page

effects.log: You keep a copy. It is a good thing to own. You find that you have rather begun to respect {him}.

choices.text: Hold the page up to a lamp, where {ot_foe} is sitting

effects.log: {ot_foe} reads it, and folds it, and thanks you. A week later {npc} finds that {his} name has been entered somewhere {he} did not expect it.

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} has been found in {his} chair with the pen in {his} hand and the day's page half done. There is no mark on {him} at all. {He} was {ot_child}'s, as everyone could read. In the book, in {his} own hand, the last entry is a debt marked paid, and the ink is still a little wet. Someone sat here with the body, and took their time.

choices.text: Say whose hand finished that line

effects.log: You say it in front of them, with {ot_foe} sitting there. It does not bring anyone back, but in this house it is written down.

choices.text: Enter the death, and close the page

effects.log: You write it yourself, in the ordinary way. A new {ot_title} will be chosen. Every lamp in the Altar burns a little lower than it needs to.

events.text: {npc} of the Red Cistern Hall wants the raids to go out again, as they did. {He} remembers when the valleys locked their doors at the colour red, and {he} thinks your heirs have turned the Cult into a place where people read. {He} will stand with whoever opens the cisterns and sends out the long raid. {He} would rather it was you.

choices.text: Send out the long raid, this season

effects.log: It goes out with drums. {He} rides at the head of it, forty years younger. The valleys lock their doors, and you are going to hear about this from a great many people.

choices.text: Ride with {him} on a small one, and show {him} what you can still do

ok.log: You are not young. You are also not nothing. {He} watches you come back over the ridge at dawn and says nothing all the way home, and in the morning {his} hall is yours.

fail.log: {He} is very kind about it on the way home. That is the worst part.

choices.text: Tell {him} those days are over

effects.log: {He} takes it well, and goes to tell the Hall what you said, in your exact words.

events.text: {npc} of the Hall of the Long Count wants every debt in the ledger to be paid in order, including one of yours. It is from a very long way back. {He} has brought the page. {He} does not threaten anything, ever. {He} simply says that an heir who would see this settled is the only heir {he} could possibly serve, and turns the page round so you can read it.

choices.text: Pay it, whatever it was

effects.log: You pay. It costs you something you do not tell anyone about, and it leaves you a few years older. {He} rules the line with great satisfaction. {He} is yours for life.

choices.text: Find the older page that cancels it

ok.log: It takes a week in the stacks, on your knees. {He} reads what you found and goes very still, and then almost smiles. No one has ever done that. {He} bows.

fail.log: There is no such page, or you could not find it. {He} waits with perfect courtesy until you have stopped looking.

choices.text: Tell {him} the Blood God owes no one

effects.log: {He} writes that down too, in the column where it belongs.

events.text: {npc} of the Left Lamp wants the altar's tithe raised, and points out that silver is a kind of tithe. {He} has an inventory of what both of your heirs have promised. {He} would so much rather be serving the Blood God directly, {he} says. {He} has written a figure on a very small piece of paper, and slides it to you with one finger.

choices.text: Pay the figure

effects.log: It goes into the Left Lamp's strongroom. {He} trims the lamp with {his} own hand, and it burns very well. It always did. (-800 taels)

choices.text: Raise the tithe on the squads instead

effects.log: They pay, and they know exactly who asked for it. {He} is yours. Your heirs both start being very sympathetic to the squads.

choices.text: Blow out the Left Lamp, and ask {him} who {he} is now

effects.log: It is a very long moment. Someone relights it. {He} goes on being correct, and you have made an enemy of the only person who knows where the money goes.

events.text: {npc} of the Right Lamp is the only person left who believes it all. {He} has kept the rites for seventy years, and has seen you yawn at them. {He} wants them kept by someone who believes, and has been watching your heirs to see if either does. Neither does. {He} comes to ask you, very simply, whether you do. {He} would know if you lied.

choices.text: Keep the long vigil with {him}, all nine nights

ok.log: On the ninth night something moves in the lamp that should not, and you both see it. Neither of you speaks of it. {He} kisses the hem of your robe in the morning, and you find you are shaking.

fail.log: You fall asleep on the fifth night. {He} covers you with {his} own robe and tells nobody, and you have your answer as well.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth: that you do not know

effects.log: {He} thinks for a long while, and then says it is the first honest thing {he} has heard on this stair. {He} will stand beside you, and pray for you. It is rather unnerving.

choices.text: Tell {him} you are the Blood God, and {he} may draw {his} own conclusion

effects.log: {He} bows. {He} has been told that before, by better. {He} goes back to {his} lamp.

events.text: You ruled the line under {ot_foe}'s name. {ot_child} has been polite since, and has asked only for an accounting: everything {ot_he} ever brought the Altar, itemised, with interest, and the question of what is owed {ot_him} now. The clerks have been working on it for a month. It is a very long document, and each line is accurate.

choices.text: Sit down with {ot_him} and go through it all, line by line

effects.log: It takes nine days. On the last day you sign it, and {ot_he} takes it and burns it without looking. Then {ot_he} asks about the salt country. You give it to {ot_him}.

choices.text: Pay {ot_him} out in full, and send {ot_him} away

effects.log: The carts leave in spring. You have paid everything you owe. {ot_He} has told people that {ot_he} considers the account still open.

choices.text: Have the clerks stop

effects.log: They stop. The document stays in the Long Count, three-quarters finished, where anyone at all might go and read it.

events.text: They have sealed the last Blood God behind the Altar with the proper rites, and nobody ruled the line. The book lies open at the page with both your columns in it. {ot_foe} has come to the Altar in full red. {ot_fHe} takes up the pen and looks at you across the lamps, and sets it down again, very gently, within reach of you both.

choices.text: Do not touch the pen. Leave it for the whole Cult to see

effects.log: You leave it there. It is a very long war, in this house, that starts with neither party writing anything. People begin to come and look at it.

choices.text: Pick it up, and write your own name again, in front of everyone

effects.log: You write it clearly. Half the hall breathes in. It does not settle anything, and now you have the first entry against you.

events.text: The Masters and the Elders will side with whoever has the better claim in the book. So the war is being fought in the Hall of the Long Count, for now, by clerks. You can go and sit up with the old ledgers looking for your parent's marks. Or you can go down to the crimson robes, who cannot read, and who have been told what the book says.

choices.text: Read until you find it

ok.log: Your parent marked one page, in a shaking hand, the winter before the end. It says nothing clear. But it is a mark, and it is beside your name, and you have it copied forty times.

fail.log: There is nothing. Or there are forty things, each meaning something else. {ot_foe}'s clerks have been faster.

choices.text: Go down to the crimson robes

effects.log: You sit at their fires. They do not care what the book says if you know their squad's dead by name. You make sure you do.

events.text: {ot_foe}'s people have taken the Cisterns and the old stair, and the crimson robes are killing each other in the corridors by the light of the Altar's own lamps. Whoever holds the Altar court at the next red night holds the rite. There are two days left, and you can see from here how few people you would have to go through.

choices.text: Take the Altar court yourself

ok.log: You stand on the Altar court at dawn, and it is yours, and you have the lamps lit. It looks very like the old paintings. It looks exactly as bad as they do.

fail.log: You are thrown back from the top step. They light the lamps without you. You can see them all the way from the lower stair.

choices.text: Hold the lower halls, and let them come down to you

effects.log: They come down. It costs them as much as it costs you. Nobody will ever paint this, but you are still here.

events.text: There is an old form for this, and neither of you has to be told it. You stand with the book between you on the Altar and all four lamps burning. The Elders have opened it to your page. Whoever walks away from this rules the line, and the other's column is closed, and everything held goes with it. The old form allows a very few other words as well.

choices.text: Stand and fight

ok.log: When it is over you can hear the lamps. {ot_foe} is on the stone. You pick up the pen with a hand that barely works and rule the line, and it is not straight.

fail.log: {ot_foe} does not hurry. You feel the stone against your face and hear the pen scratch. It is a very clean line, and you can read it from there.

choices.text: Offer to enter both names, one above the other, with a price agreed

ok.log: No one has done this since the second Blood God, and they did it badly. {ot_foe} reads the terms twice. You sign first, on the upper line. It is the most expensive thing you will ever buy.

fail.log: {ot_foe} reads it, and sets it aside, and says it is a very interesting document. It will be the stone next year, and {ot_fhe} has a copy of your offer now.

choices.text: Cross out your own column

effects.log: You do it yourself. It takes one stroke. The Elders look at you with something you would like to think is respect.

events.text: {ot_foe} is alive. The column is closed, and the old form says only that a closed column has no further claim on anything, including breath. The Elders wait for you to say what that means this time. Every one of them has a long memory. They are not at all sure what they want you to do, and they are going to write down what you do.

choices.text: Enter {ot_foe} as a debtor to the Altar, and let {ot_fhim} serve

effects.log: {ot_fHe} takes up a clerk's stool in the Long Count. It is alive, and it is not nothing. It is also a very long way down.

choices.text: Send {ot_fhim} away, with the debt marked unpaid

effects.log: {ot_fHe} goes down the old road with nothing, and the entry stays open. The book is patient.

choices.text: Let the old form mean what it says

effects.log: It means what it says. You write that entry yourself, and the ink does not dry as quickly as it should. There are nights now when you check the page.

events.text: Your column is closed. {ot_foe} has ruled the line. The Elders have brought you the page to look at, as is proper. Nobody has yet said what it means this time. They are very old, and they do not mind waiting. You could make it easier for them, or you could go now, while the lamps are all looking the other way.

choices.text: Kneel and enter yourself in the Altar's service

effects.log: You sign where they show you. There is a seat among the Elders' clerks, and then, in time, among the Elders. You keep your eyes on your own page.

choices.text: Go, by the old drain, under the Cisterns

effects.log: It is the way you found when you were nine. It still goes through. You come out in the cold with the red washed off you, and you do not know yet who that leaves.

events.text: You keep a Hall of the Blood Cult, and your name is in the book in a place that matters. So {ot_child} and {ot_foe}, of the blood of the one above you, have each sent a clerk. Each has brought a very accurate summary of what you are owed and by whom, and a proposal to pay it. In this house, there is no warmer way of asking.

choices.text: Accept {ot_child}'s accounting

effects.log: You initial it. It is a very fair sum. You now appear on a page you will not be able to get off.

choices.text: Accept {ot_foe}'s accounting

effects.log: You initial it. The clerk bows and blots it carefully, and you have become an asset.

choices.text: Find an error in each of them, and send them back

effects.log: You find one in each. There is always one. They will both come back with more, and neither of them has your name yet.

events.text: The lamps have been lit at the wrong hour, and that means the one above you is near the end. A clerk from your chosen heir has brought you a page: the list of those who will be standing at the Altar tonight, your name already written in, in a fair hand, with a small space left for your mark.

choices.text: Sign, and stand there in full red

effects.log: You go, with everyone you have. It cannot be erased now, and you find that is a relief.

choices.text: Sign, in a thin ink, and send your deputy

effects.log: It is a very careful thing to do. It is also a thing that the book has a column for.

events.text: In the ghost city the dead walk at night in their long lines, and the living stand aside. This month the Night Parade has been walking with two lanterns at its head, where it has only ever had one. Nobody ordered it. {ot_child} walks beside one, {ot_foe} beside the other, each very calm. The bell-keeper has asked you, in a whisper, which one the dead are meant to follow.

choices.text: Walk at the head yourself, with no lantern at all

effects.log: You walk the whole road in the dark, at the front. The dead come after you. It is the quietest thing you have ever done, and everyone in the city has heard of it by dawn.

choices.text: Tell the bell-keeper the dead will decide

effects.log: That goes round the city in a night. The white-robed start to watch the lines to see which is longer.

events.text: It is the Hour of Names, when the sect reads out those who are to be carried and those who will carry. Someone has written a third list. It is short, and has only your heirs on it, {ot_child} and {ot_foe}, under the words 'To Keep the Chair.' It was found on the white chair itself, with an urn set on it to hold it down. You sat on that chair this morning. It was not there then.

choices.text: Read it out with the others, as if it were ordinary

effects.log: You read it in your ordinary voice. The silence goes on a long time. Nobody can say you did not know of it.

choices.text: Put it in the urn, and have the urn sealed

effects.log: You seal it. It goes on a shelf in the Urn House, where anyone may read the label: {ot_seat}, and a date.

events.text: {ot_child} prefers the company of the dead, and they ask nothing. But the Keeper of the Lanterns has begun leaving a small white lantern at {ot_his} door, a little nearer each week. When {ot_he} asked about it, the Keeper said only that a road must have someone on it, and that {ot_foe} is on it alone. {ot_He} came to you and said that {ot_he} would like not to be seen. {ot_He} meant it.

choices.text: Have the lanterns taken away, by your own hand

effects.log: You carry them off yourself, four nights running. {ot_child} watches from the window. On the fifth night it is still there, but {ot_he} thanks you all the same.

choices.text: Tell {ot_him} nobody here is unseen

effects.log: {ot_He} thinks it over, and picks up the lantern. You did not know how much you liked the way {ot_he} used to walk until {ot_he} stopped.

events.text: The families of nine prefectures send to the Ashen Ghosts to have their dead walked home. {ot_child} has walked forty this season, and people have begun asking for {ot_him} by name. {ot_foe} has walked only one, but it was a dead general over the mountains in midwinter, with the whole of his old army lined up to watch. Your clerks are getting very tired of being asked who is better at it.

choices.text: Forbid any bearer to be asked for by name

effects.log: It holds for a year. Then the families start asking for the one with the steady hands, or the one with the voice, and they all know who is meant.

choices.text: Send {ot_foe} on the next great walk too

effects.log: It is a very splendid walk. {ot_child} sends you a very respectful list of the forty names.

events.text: At the Lantern Feast, the white lanterns are floated down the black canal, and it is held to be lucky if yours goes the furthest. It is a children's custom. This year {ot_child}'s lantern and {ot_foe}'s went further than any lantern ever has, side by side, and they are still going. The whole of the ghost city is out on the banks, not saying anything, watching them go.

choices.text: Have a boat sent out to fetch both in

effects.log: The boat comes back with both of them, unlit. Nobody cheers. You are told that it was a very wise decision.

choices.text: Go home. It is a children's custom

effects.log: You go home. In the morning people say one of them reached the sea. They do not agree which, and they have begun to fight about it.

events.text: {ot_foe} has learned the Corpse-Bell Palm to its last form, and shows it at the winter gathering. It is very cold in the hall for some time afterwards. {ot_child} does not answer. {ot_He} goes to see old Keepers on their deathbeds, one by one, and sits with them, and comes away knowing where each has hidden something. It is not clear to you which of these is the more dangerous.

choices.text: Ask {ot_child} what {ot_he} has been told

effects.log: {ot_He} tells you a little of it, watching your face. You realise that you are also being sat with.

choices.text: Praise {ot_foe}'s palm, in front of the hall

effects.log: The cold goes on a little longer than it needs to. {ot_child} is at a bedside, and does not look up when {ot_he} hears of it.

events.text: A family in Dali has come to you in tears. Their grandfather's urn, walked home by {ot_child}'s people, has the wrong ash in it. A few days later so does another family's, and a third. The Ashen Ghosts have many sins, and nobody has ever once said that of them. Someone has been changing urns on the road, and every urn has been on {ot_child}'s list.

choices.text: Go through the Urn House's records, seal by seal

ok.log: The seals were cut this spring, by someone who has a very good eye and a key to {ot_foe}'s storeroom. The families have their dead back, and you have a page you do not read out.

fail.log: It is well done. The seals are all good, and the ash is all wrong, and {ot_child}'s name is on every page.

choices.text: Pay the families, and walk the dead home again yourself

effects.log: You walk them yourself. It costs you a winter and a good deal of silver, and the story changes on the way. (-400 taels)

events.text: The Keeper of the Bell tells you that it has been tolled for {ot_foe}. It was tolled only once, at the third hour, by no one, and half of the city woke up and heard it. {ot_foe} is alive and in excellent health. Somebody has been paying for the rumour, and a great many people have stopped looking {ot_fhim} in the eye. In this city that is the one thing you cannot buy back.

choices.text: Have {ot_foe} walk the main street at noon, beside you

effects.log: It is an unusual thing to see here. People open their shutters. {ot_fHe} walks very straight, and {ot_fhe} does not forget who had to be there to make it believed.

choices.text: Find out who has the tower key

effects.log: You do. It leads to a young man who is very frightened of something, and it is not you. You give it a while.

events.text: A letter reaches you, in a hand that is very like {ot_foe}'s, from someone in the Wudang Sect, your people's old enemy. It offers thanks for certain maps of the southern road. It reached you by way of three helpful friends. You note that the paper is older than the ink. You note, too, that this is the sort of thing you would only be meant to notice if you were clever.

choices.text: Show it to {ot_foe}, and watch

effects.log: {ot_fHe} reads it, and looks at you, and says the paper is older than the ink. It may be that {ot_fhe} is innocent. It may be that {ot_fhe} has read this far ahead.

choices.text: Put it in the Urn House, and let it be known it is there

effects.log: Nobody asks to see it. Everyone knows the shelf. It works on all of them, a little, like cold.

events.text: {ot_child} came back from the night road with frost on {ot_his} shoulders in midsummer. Someone had been walking behind {ot_him} in the line, one of the dead, with a very live hand. {ot_He} has a mark on {ot_his} back in the exact shape of the Corpse-Bell Palm and is keeping very warm. Only a few people know that form. {ot_foe} has had some very good ginger sent over.

choices.text: Have every bearer on the road counted, living and dead

effects.log: It takes a week. The count comes out one too many, and then, on the second try, just right. {ot_foe} sends more ginger.

choices.text: Sit with {ot_child} until the cold goes out of {ot_him}

effects.log: You put your own qi into it, night after night. It leaves you tired for a year. {ot_He} says nothing about it. {ot_He} leaves a white flower on your desk.

events.text: {ot_foe}'s room was full of incense this morning, of a kind that is burned only for the dead, and {ot_fhe} was very nearly asleep for good. A servant noticed that the door was warm. There is no way to tell how it got in. Whoever did this knew {ot_fhe} sleeps alone with the window shut, and that is a thing {ot_fhe} told only one other person, a long time ago, when they were both small.

choices.text: Ask {ot_child} what {ot_he} remembers of being small

effects.log: {ot_He} tells you a story of the two of them on the canal, and it is lovely. You do not know if that is an answer. You believe it was meant to be.

choices.text: Have the servant who noticed raised to Keeper of the door

effects.log: The whole city sees what noticing is worth. It will not stop anyone, but they will be careful around that door.

events.text: Tonight the Night Parade met itself. {ot_child}'s bearers came up the White Lantern Road with their line of dead, and {ot_foe}'s bearers came down it, and they stopped, in the rain, a foot apart. Nobody here is shouting. It does not make it better. People have started to fight in complete silence with the dead standing all around them, and the lanterns are going out one at a time.

choices.text: Ring the great bell with your own hand

ok.log: It has not rung at this hour in living memory, and they stop, and the dead stop too. You stand in the tower holding the rope. You are not sure you could have done it twice.

fail.log: It rings, and some of them stop. By the morning you can count by the lanterns who did not.

choices.text: Leave them be. Count the lanterns at dawn

effects.log: At dawn you count them, and there are many more on one side. It is done as quietly as it was fought. The city goes on being very polite.

events.text: {ot_foe} has shut up the Urn House, with the ashes of nine prefectures in it, and is receiving the families personally. {ot_child} has shut the Bell Tower, and nobody in the city now knows who has died. People are being carried past each other in the street with no one sure who has the right to do it. Your own people have started asking whether you have a plan, in very low voices.

choices.text: Open the Urn House in your own name, and the Tower too

effects.log: You go, alone, in white. They open. They were always going to open for you, and that is not the same as it being over.

choices.text: Back {ot_foe}, and let the Bell Tower go hungry

effects.log: It takes the Tower a month to come down. It has started to matter now which side the dead are on.

events.text: All the Keepers have come to you, in the white, at the Hour of Names. They do not raise their voices. The eldest says only that the sect has walked every kind of dead there is, and it has not yet had to walk a whole city. They have brought a lantern, unlit, and they set it at your feet. {ot_child} is strongest, and {ot_foe} just behind. Nobody looks at either one.

choices.text: Light it, and hand it to {ot_child}

effects.log: It lights the first time. {ot_child} takes it without a word, and the line forms up behind {ot_him}, and it goes on for a long way. You feel very cold.

choices.text: Have {ot_foe} walked out of the city, alive, with the dead behind {ot_fhim}

effects.log: It is the oldest of your punishments: to be treated as already gone. Nobody will speak to {ot_fhim} ever again. {ot_fHe} looks back once.

choices.text: Leave it unlit

effects.log: They wait a long time, and then they pick it up and go. A month later {ot_foe} walks out of the west gate with a third of the Keepers, and now there are two ghost cities.

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} has hung a second lantern at {his} door, a small one, with {ot_child}'s mark on the paper. That is all. In the ghost city that is a declaration. {He} says, if asked, that {ot_child} has the right sort of patience and may be able to give {him} what {he} wants, which is {ot_want}. {He} is not often asked. People have started to cross the street.

choices.text: Walk past it, and nod to the lantern

effects.log: You nod, and it is seen. One more door in the city has declared itself, and nobody can say you were not told.

choices.text: Send a very old lantern as a gift, for that door

effects.log: It is a great honour. It is rather larger than the small one, and there is only one hook. {He} takes the hint, and it is the old lantern that stays up. (-300 taels)

events.text: The funeral silver of nine prefectures runs through {ot_hall}, and lately a little more of it has been staying there. Your listener followed a small chest from {ot_child}'s rooms, by way of a coffin that had nobody in it. {npc} has been receiving empty coffins for most of a year, and is known throughout the city for {his} piety.

choices.text: Send {him} a heavier coffin

effects.log: It arrives with your seal on the inside of the lid. {He} says a very long prayer over it, and {ot_child}'s next one is sent back unopened. (-400 taels)

choices.text: Let {him} know how many coffins you have counted

effects.log: A small slip of paper with a number is left on {his} altar. It is the right number. {He} burns incense for a whole day.

events.text: In the ghost city a wedding is held at night, in white, and it is thought lucky if the dead attend. {npc} of {ot_hall} has given {his} heir to {ot_child}, and the whole Night Parade has been asked to walk past the door. It is a great many dead for a wedding, and it is meant to be counted from the walls. It looks very beautiful, and {ot_foe} has sent a lantern.

choices.text: Attend, and be the first to bow

effects.log: You bow. You have walked past a good many things in this life, and this may be the coldest. That door has a family now, and it is on one side.

choices.text: Have the omens read, by someone who needs money

effects.log: The omens are dreadful. Nobody will marry at that door for a generation. {npc} knows exactly what the reading cost. (-500 taels)

events.text: Your listener says {npc} of {ot_hall} still hangs {ot_foe}'s lantern, and still tells {ot_fhim} all that the dead tell {him}. But for most of this year {he} has been telling it to {ot_child} first, by way of an old woman who sells paper money. It is carefully done. {ot_foe} has not noticed anything. You suppose that it will come as a surprise, at a very bad time.

choices.text: Leave it be, and buy a little paper money

effects.log: You pay the old woman very well. Now it goes through three hands, and the third one is yours.

choices.text: Have the old woman moved to another street

effects.log: The old woman goes, with a nice pension. {ot_child} does not ask where. {npc} starts hanging {his} lantern a little crooked, which you take to mean something.

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} was {ot_child}'s, and this morning {he} joined the Night Parade. {He} was seen in the line, walking with {his} eyes open, by several people who knew {him} well. The physician says {he} has been dead since the evening before. Nobody can say who raised {him}, though it is not a thing many people here can do. It has been very clearly meant as a message.

choices.text: Name who can do this, in front of them all

effects.log: It is a very short list, and {ot_foe} is on it. You read it at the Hour of Names. Then you walk {npc} home, as {he} deserves.

choices.text: Have {him} laid down with all the rites, and say no more

effects.log: {He} is laid down properly, and nobody mentions it. It is a very good funeral. In the ghost city, they take that to mean you were frightened.

events.text: {npc} of the Night Parade wants the procession to walk further than it has been let to. For thirty years it has stopped at the border of the ghost city. {He} says there are a great many dead on the other side who would come, if called, and {ot_child} and {ot_foe} have both promised to call them. {He} is a very gentle person, and you have never been sure if {he} is joking.

choices.text: Let the Parade walk to the next prefecture, once

effects.log: It goes out one night in the rain. Whole towns close their doors and say prayers. It comes back very much longer than it left, and {he} is entirely yours.

choices.text: Walk the border with {him} and show {him} why it stands there

ok.log: You walk it all night. By the third hour {he} has fallen silent. In the morning {he} says that no one had ever shown {him} what was on the other side of it, and {he} has been yours since.

fail.log: {He} listens with great gentleness. You come home knowing more about the border than you wanted to. {He} has not changed {his} mind at all.

choices.text: Tell {him} the border stands

effects.log: {He} smiles, and thanks you, and goes back to {his} line. It seems a little longer than it was.

events.text: {npc} of the Bell Tower wants to hear who has died before the family does. {He} has always been able to. It has lately been failing, because your heirs have people who get there first. {He} has come to ask you for a small thing: the first word, from all your networks and all your roads. {He} will tell you, in exchange, who is going to die next. {He} has a very good record.

choices.text: Agree, and ask who is next

effects.log: {He} tells you. It is nobody you know. A month later, you do know, and you find you did not want this after all. {He} is yours.

choices.text: Ask {him} when the bell will ring for you

effects.log: {He} looks at you for a long time. Then {he} tells you. You will not repeat it, and neither will {he}. It is an odd thing to have in common, and it holds.

choices.text: Tell {him} the bell rings when you say

effects.log: {He} bows. As {he} goes out you can hear it starting, just faintly, for someone.

events.text: {npc} of the Urn House wants the funeral silver of nine prefectures left unexamined. It is a remarkably large sum. {He} points out, with care, that if it were ever examined it would turn out that this chair has been drawing on it too, for generations. {He} has both your heirs' signatures in {his} sleeve, and {he} would prefer yours. {He} names a modest price for the trouble.

choices.text: Pay the modest price

effects.log: {He} shows you where to sign. The Urn House is yours, and you have never been so close to the thing you always told people you were not. (-800 taels)

choices.text: Examine it anyway, all of it, yourself

ok.log: It takes a season. You find what {he} did, and what the chair did. You have both written out and hand {him} one of the copies. {He} sees what you mean. {He} serves you very faithfully after that.

fail.log: It is very well hidden. You are still looking when the snow comes, and {he} sends in hot soup.

choices.text: Tell {him} you will think about it

effects.log: {He} is very happy to wait. {He} has been waiting for a long time, and most of the people {he} waits for are already in {his} care.

events.text: {npc} of the White Lantern Road wants nobody living to walk it who has not earned it. Both of your heirs have been walking it at night, trying to be seen. {He} has come to ask for the old test to be held again, the one where you walk the road to its end, alone, without a lantern, and come back. {He} points out, without any emphasis, that you have never done it yourself.

choices.text: Walk it

ok.log: It is further than you thought. Somewhere near the end, somebody you used to know walks beside you for a while. You come back at dawn with white in your hair, and {he} is waiting, and {he} bows to the ground.

fail.log: You turn back. You are not sure where. {He} is there when you get home, and {he} offers you {his} arm, and never says a word to anyone.

choices.text: Order that nobody of the blood walks it until the test is held

effects.log: {He} inclines {his} head. It is a good law, and it stops your heirs, for now. {He} is yours, and neither of them will thank you.

choices.text: Tell {him} the road is yours, and so is everyone on it

effects.log: {He} agrees completely. {He} goes on walking it, and so do they.

events.text: You put the lantern in {ot_foe}'s hand. {ot_child} carried {ot_his} own lantern to the Urn House the next morning and left it, unlit, on the shelf with the sealed things. {ot_He} has not spoken since, not to anyone. {ot_His} people have begun coming to the Hour of Names and standing at the back, also saying nothing. It is very hard to find a charge against that.

choices.text: Go and stand beside {ot_him} at the back

effects.log: You stand there three nights. On the third {ot_he} speaks, and it is to ask if {ot_he} may have the far road, in the south. You say yes. {ot_He} takes the lantern down.

choices.text: Have {ot_him} walked out of the west gate

effects.log: {ot_He} goes, without a word, with those who stood at the back. Nobody here will ever mention {ot_him} again. It is what is done here.

choices.text: Leave {ot_him} there

effects.log: The silence goes on. The back of the hall gets more crowded, and {ot_foe} has begun to look over {ot_fhis} shoulder when {ot_fhe} speaks.

events.text: They walked your parent home tonight, a long white line, and nobody was holding the lantern. It had not been done before. Halfway down the canal {ot_foe} stepped out and took up a lantern of {ot_fhis} own, and the line slowed. You are close enough to see {ot_fhis} face. The white chair stands empty behind you both, and the Keepers are looking at your hands.

choices.text: Light your own, and walk beside {ot_fhim}, a pace ahead

effects.log: You walk the whole way. Nobody says anything. It is a very long line, and by the end there are two lines in it.

choices.text: Carry the bier yourself, with no lantern

effects.log: You take a corner of it, and your shoulder hurts for a week. People in the crowd saw that, and some of them are bearers.

events.text: A Keeper will not come to you for silver or for a speech. You have until the Hour of Names to give them some reason. You could go to the deathbeds of the old ones, as the clever do, and learn where everything is. Or you could go and walk the long roads with the bearers, in the rain, carrying what they carry, until they begin to walk behind you.

choices.text: Sit at the deathbeds

ok.log: You sit nine nights with nine old people. One of them tells you where the second key is, and then asks you to hold her hand. You do both.

fail.log: They are very old and they know what you are doing. One of them laughs until it nearly finishes her.

choices.text: Walk with the bearers

effects.log: You walk until your boots give out. They begin to save you a place in the line. It is not a very high place, but it is real.

events.text: {ot_foe}'s people hold the Bell Tower, and whoever holds that says who is dead, and tonight they have tolled for you. People you have known for years are avoiding your eye on the bridges. You must be seen. There is one street that goes up to the Tower, with nothing on it but white lanterns, and you could walk straight up the middle.

choices.text: Walk up the middle of the street

ok.log: They come out at you from the doorways, and you keep walking. At the Tower you take the rope yourself, and you ring it for nobody. The whole city hears it, and it knows who rang it.

fail.log: You get as far as the steps. They carry you back down the street on a board, and people are very respectful about it. It looks a great deal like a funeral.

choices.text: Stay away from the Tower and go round the houses by night

effects.log: You knock on every door that will open, and you let them touch your hand. It is slow. It is a good answer to a bell, though not the best.

events.text: At the end of the White Lantern Road, where nobody goes, two lamps have been set down. {ot_foe} is already there, in white. There are no witnesses but the ones who cannot speak, and there are a great many of them. Whoever comes back along this road alone will sit the chair. The other will be walked home in the proper way, and everything you hold is staked on it.

choices.text: Set down your coat

ok.log: It is very quiet, and very cold, and then it is over. You walk back alone, with the dead on both sides. They do not look at you, and you take that as a kind of approval.

fail.log: You wake up on the road, and it is morning. {ot_foe} has left you a lantern, lit, and gone on ahead. Somewhere behind you the bell begins.

choices.text: Say that you will walk the far road for life, if {ot_fhe} will keep the Tower under you

ok.log: You talk until the lamps burn low. It may be that {ot_fhe} is as tired as you are. In the end {ot_fhe} takes your lamp, and hands you back the larger one. The chair is yours.

fail.log: {ot_fHe} listens, and picks up {ot_fhis} lamp, and walks back without a word. It will be here again next year. You have shown {ot_fhim} you are afraid of the road.

choices.text: Pick up your lamp, and walk the other way

effects.log: There is another way. It goes on for a long time. {ot_foe} watches you go, and neither of you has to say anything.

events.text: You came back alone, or as near as makes no difference, because {ot_foe} is not dead. {ot_fHe} is lying out on the road, and a bearer has come to you to ask what is to be done. The Keepers will not look up. You know the two usual answers. There is a third that was your parent's, and you do not know if it was meant kindly.

choices.text: Bring {ot_fhim} in, and give {ot_fhim} the far southern road to keep

effects.log: {ot_fHe} keeps it for years, without a word to you, and very well. It is either forgiveness or a very long patience. You light a lamp for {ot_fhim} at the feast.

choices.text: Have {ot_fhim} carried out past the west gate

effects.log: They carry {ot_fhim} out at dawn and set {ot_fhim} down. Nobody here will speak of {ot_fhim} again. {ot_fHe} is, for every purpose here, already gone.

choices.text: Let the road have {ot_fhim}

effects.log: You tell the bearer to go home. In the morning there is one more in the Parade, walking very straight, and you find you cannot look at the front of the line.

events.text: They rang the bell for you at dawn, and you heard it, which was not supposed to happen. {ot_foe} has the white chair. You are still alive, as far as it goes. In the ghost city it can go a long way, and you have an idea what your choices are: to live among them as one who is no longer spoken of, or to go somewhere people have never heard the bell.
