choices.text: Bow to {ot_foe}, and stay, among the Keepers' clerks

effects.log: {ot_fHe} does not look at you. Somebody finds you a stool, and a brush. In time, some of them may start to speak to you.

choices.text: Take the south road, and do not look back

effects.log: You walk until the lanterns are yellow. A child offers you a bun, and you have forgotten how to take one. You are going to have to learn.

events.text: You keep a post in the ghost city. So there are two small white lanterns on your step this morning, and you know whose: {ot_child} and {ot_foe}, of the blood of the one who sits the chair. Nobody has knocked. Nobody will. You need only take one in and leave the other for the rain, and it will be known by nightfall. If you leave them both, that will be known as well.

choices.text: Take in {ot_child}'s lantern

effects.log: You hang it by the door. It is an elegant thing. In the evening, a very small gift appears on your sill.

choices.text: Take in {ot_foe}'s lantern

effects.log: You hang it by the door. In the morning the other has gone, and there is a white flower where it stood, which might be a threat.

choices.text: Leave them both out in the rain

effects.log: They go out one after the other. You stand and watch them. You are going to be very much alone in this city, and it is very safe to be alone here, up to a point.

events.text: The chair is going to be empty soon. The whole city knows that because the bell-keeper has started looking at the one who sits there in a certain way. Your lantern has been sent for. It is the night you always knew about: when each door in the ghost city must carry out what it hung up, and stand in the line, and be counted.

choices.text: Walk at the front, where it will be seen

effects.log: You go out in full white, with your people behind you. Nobody could ever say you were not there.

choices.text: Walk near the back, in the rain, and keep your lantern low

effects.log: It is prudent. You can still see everything from there. So can the ones who count.

events.text: A memorial has come up from the Ministry of Rites, respectfully noting that the Heir's Palace has stood empty for some years and that its roof needs mending. It is four pages on roof tiles. Everyone at court has read it. By evening there are two parties of officials who have strong opinions on tiles, and one party dines with {ot_child} and the other with {ot_foe}.

choices.text: Approve the repair, and house nobody there

effects.log: The roof is mended beautifully. The empty palace now shines in the sun where the whole court can see it from the morning audience.

choices.text: Have the memorial returned, unread, with your thanks

effects.log: It comes back in a month with a different title. But for a month the court has been careful.

events.text: It is the custom that the Emperor's children stand at the Winter Sacrifice in the order of their standing. Nobody has ever had to write the order down. The Master of Ceremonies has come to you in some distress, with a chart. He has moved {ot_child} a pace forward and {ot_foe} a pace back, then the reverse, nine times, and the paper has worn through. There are two days left.

choices.text: Have them stand side by side

effects.log: They stand side by side. The whole court spends the Sacrifice looking at the inch between them, and the Censorate writes down whose foot was forward.

choices.text: Put {ot_child} a pace forward and say nothing

effects.log: It is one pace. By the New Year it has become a policy, and {ot_foe} has been seen reading the old histories of second sons and daughters.

events.text: {ot_child} has asked for nothing but a quiet post in the Imperial Library. It has not helped. The Minister of Rites has discovered that {ot_his} birth was unusually auspicious, and three officials have come to the Library to consult {ot_him} on a point of no importance. {ot_foe} must not be allowed to stand unopposed, they explain, for the good of the realm. They have brought the proper robes.

choices.text: Tell them {ot_child} is not to be consulted

effects.log: They bow very low and go away. Then they begin consulting {ot_his} tutor. {ot_child} sends you a very good book.

choices.text: Let {ot_child} try on the robes

effects.log: They fit. Someone had {ot_his} measurements. {ot_He} looks in the mirror for a while, and you never again hear {ot_him} talk about the Library.

events.text: The flood on the Yellow River has given {ot_child} a chance to be seen in mud to the waist, with a great many officials taking notes. {ot_foe} has stayed at the capital and found the grain to feed them, and sees that this is known too. The people have started singing about {ot_child}. The Ministry of Revenue has started paying its bills to {ot_foe}. Both of these are in today's report.

choices.text: Praise them both in one edict

effects.log: It is a very balanced edict. Scholars will study its adjectives for years, starting tonight.

choices.text: Give the flood commission to {ot_foe} as well

effects.log: The dykes get built, by two sets of engineers, on opposite banks. They are excellent dykes.

events.text: There has been a poetry gathering at the Moon Pavilion. {ot_foe}'s verse on the plum tree was admired by all. {ot_child}'s verse on the plum tree was admired by more, and there is reason to think it was admired on account of a line about old trees and the shade they keep from young ones. It is a very good line. The whole capital can recite it, and your name is not in it anywhere.

choices.text: Answer with a verse of your own

effects.log: You send one down, about the gardener. It is not a good poem. It ends all discussion of the plum tree for some time.

choices.text: Have the line explained to you, by {ot_child}, in person

effects.log: {ot_He} explains it for an hour, perfectly at ease, about plum trees. You have both enjoyed it very much, and neither of you has blinked.

events.text: Foreign envoys have arrived, and there is the matter of who receives them. {ot_child} is said to speak the western tongue. {ot_foe} is said to have made a study of their horses. The envoys, who are no fools, have brought two sets of presents of carefully equal value, and have asked very politely which of the Emperor's children they ought to remember to their own ruler.

choices.text: Receive them yourself, and take both sets

effects.log: You are a magnificent host. The envoys go home and report that the question is still open, which is what they most wanted to know.

choices.text: Let {ot_foe} receive them

effects.log: It goes very well. Next year there are western horses in {ot_foe}'s stable, and a western friend writing to {ot_fhim} directly.

events.text: The Censorate has presented a formal impeachment of a Vice Minister close to {ot_child}, on forty counts. Thirty-nine are nonsense. The fortieth is that he kept in his desk a list of officials to be promoted at the start of a new reign, in a hand that may be {ot_child}'s. Everyone in the audience hall is looking at the floor with enormous attention.

choices.text: Send for the desk, and read the list yourself

ok.log: The list is real, and the paper has come from {ot_foe}'s own stationer. You return the impeachment with one sentence in the margin. {ot_foe} has a quiet month.

fail.log: It may be {ot_child}'s hand. It may be anyone's. You have now asked, in front of the entire court.

choices.text: Dismiss the Vice Minister, and let the rest drop

effects.log: He goes to a far province with his whole family. {ot_child} has lost one good man, and has noted which one of you did it.

events.text: A rumour has reached the markets that {ot_foe} was not born when the records say, and that the Rites Ministry has amended a page. It has been printed on very cheap paper, and it is very well written. Three booksellers have been arrested, and they all bought it from a man with a northern accent who paid in new silver. The court physicians have stopped making eye contact with {ot_foe}'s mother's family.

choices.text: Have the original register brought out and shown in public

effects.log: It is carried through the capital in a yellow sedan with a hundred guards. Nothing could have made the rumour better known. It is, at least, disproved.

choices.text: Double the guard at the printers, and look for the silver

effects.log: It leads through two eunuchs and a salt merchant, to a door you already suspected.

events.text: Your ears at court report that the two sides have started to compete in loyalty to you. Each sends up memorials, day after day, praising your health. Each has begun to ask, out of the deepest concern, which physician attends you and what he has prescribed. You are starting to have a very clear idea of how you look from the outside.

choices.text: Announce that you have never been better, and go hunting

effects.log: You kill a very large stag, and it nearly kills you. The memorials change the subject for a while.

choices.text: Have your physician replaced in secret, and tell no one

effects.log: He goes on attending you, as far as they know. There is a second man now, who has never heard of either party.

events.text: {ot_child}'s carriage lost a wheel on the Jade Bridge, at a height that would have been the end of most people. {ot_He} was thrown clear. The pin had been sawn through very neatly. The Commandant of the Capital Guard has arrested the wheelwright, who has hanged himself in his cell, in a manner that would have required a much taller wheelwright. {ot_foe} has sent to enquire after {ot_his} health.

choices.text: Remove the Commandant, and give the case to the Censorate

effects.log: A whole department now has a reason to find the truth, and another has a reason to stop them. It may come out in the wash.

choices.text: Assign {ot_child} your own guards

effects.log: Your own guards march beside {ot_his} carriage from now on. The whole capital sees whose carriage it is.

events.text: A taster has died at {ot_foe}'s table. {ot_fHe} went on to finish the meal from a different dish, and then wrote to you about it in a very firm hand, without one word of accusation. By custom such a letter should be answered within three days. Any answer will be read by four thousand people. The cook who prepared the dish was, until last winter, in {ot_child}'s employ.

choices.text: Answer in your own hand: come and dine with me, both of you

effects.log: They come. You eat from the same dish, the three of you, and everyone keeps up a conversation about the harvest. It is the longest meal of your reign.

choices.text: Have the cook found, and brought to you alive

effects.log: It takes a month, and it is the first thing you have ever got the Eastern Depot to do quickly. He says very little. It is enough to frighten someone.

events.text: Two companies of the Palace Guard have fought at the Gate of Heavenly Purity over a question of who had the right to pass. Each was protecting one of your heirs. The dead have been carried off, and the blood has been washed from the marble, but the ministers have come in by the side gate all week. In the markets they have started storing rice.

choices.text: Ride through the gate in full dragon robes, unguarded

ok.log: They fall on their faces from one end of the avenue to the other. There are still a few things left that cannot be done in front of you. You feel very tired afterwards.

fail.log: They bow, some a beat late. You see who, and they see you see, and you do not know yet what to do about it.

choices.text: Move the Northern Army up to the capital

effects.log: It restores order at once. You now have three parties at court, and one of them has forty thousand men.

events.text: {ot_child} holds the Eastern Palace, and {ot_foe} holds the Treasury, and both swear it is for your protection. Memorials arrive in two sets, each denouncing the other in identical language. A minister you have known for thirty years has come in, weeping, to ask you to do something, and has gone away with nothing. You can see the smoke from your window. It is only a warehouse, so far.

choices.text: Issue an edict confining them both to their residences

effects.log: It goes out under the great seal. They both obey, within the letter of it. Their residences have got a good deal larger.

choices.text: Send the Palace Guard to clear the Treasury for {ot_child}

effects.log: It is done by nightfall, and the whole court knows now which way you lean. Half of them go home to burn some letters.

events.text: The Grand Council has requested an audience at an hour when no one requests audiences. They kneel, every one of them, and they do not rise. The Chief Censor has a sealed memorial in both hands, with his own death warrant attached, as the old form allows. It says: Heaven does not leave its throne empty, and Your Majesty must speak. {ot_child} is the stronger. {ot_foe} is not far behind.

choices.text: Name {ot_child} Heir, by edict, today

effects.log: It takes only as long as the ink needs. The bells start to ring. {ot_foe}'s people are at their desks, all of them, and they are very quiet.

choices.text: Strip {ot_foe} of every title and office

effects.log: It reads as a very short decree. Then {ot_foe}'s name is no longer used at court, and you have told everybody what you can do to your own blood.

choices.text: Burn the memorial, and send them home

effects.log: They rise, slowly. Before the year is out, {ot_foe} has gone to the southern capital, with a third of the court, to protect it for you.

events.text: {npc}, {ot_title}, has been seen in {ot_child}'s garden. {He} has told everyone that it was to look at the peonies. {He} has also told those who ask that {ot_child} is one of the few who understands what the realm needs, by which {he} means {ot_want}. In the language of the court, that is the same as raising a banner. {ot_foe} has sent {him} a rare peony.

choices.text: Ask {him} about the peonies

effects.log: {He} tells you all about them for an hour. You have made your point, and {he} has made {his}. One more ministry stands with {ot_child}, in full view.

choices.text: Promote {him} to something a long way from that garden

effects.log: It is a great honour, and there is a banquet. {He} goes to take up {his} new duties, and leaves {his} peonies with a very small sigh. (-300 taels)

events.text: Your Eastern Depot has noticed {npc}'s third son is suddenly repaying some debts of a very large size. It all leads to a house owned by the wife of a man who manages {ot_child}'s estates. {npc}, {ot_title}, is a person of unblemished record. In fact, {he} has just sent up a memorial on the subject of corruption.

choices.text: Pay the son's debts before {ot_child} can

effects.log: They are paid, with a note. {npc} reads it and sits for some time, and then finds that {his} duties leave {him} no time to see {ot_child}. (-400 taels)

choices.text: Let {him} know the Depot can count

effects.log: One of your men asks {him} about it, in passing, in a corridor, with great respect. {He} goes on as before, only more nervously.

events.text: The Ministry of Rites has the honour to report that an alliance has been proposed between the house of {npc}, {ot_title}, and {ot_child}. The bride-price has been agreed, the astrologers are enthusiastic, and {ot_hall} has already started addressing {ot_child} in a slightly different tone. It requires only your seal. Declining would need a reason, and everybody is very curious to hear it.

choices.text: Seal it

effects.log: It is the wedding of the decade. {ot_foe} attends in excellent spirits and starts asking who else has daughters and sons.

choices.text: Have the astrologers find a difficulty

effects.log: They find a very serious one, for which they are well paid. Nobody believes it for a moment. {npc} bows, and you can see that {he} has made a note. (-500 taels)

events.text: It has taken your people some time to read this. {npc}, {ot_title}, still sends {ot_foe} every copy of every report. But the copies have been a day late for a year now, and in that day they have been going through {ot_child}'s hands. {ot_foe} has lost three small appointments in that time and has never understood why. You are obliged to admire the civil service.

choices.text: Leave it. Have copies made for you as well

effects.log: They now pass through three hands. {npc} may be the only person in the empire who is having a good time.

choices.text: Let {ot_foe} find out, at the morning audience

effects.log: You ask {npc} a question about a date. {He} answers it correctly, and {ot_foe} goes white. Then {he} is ill for a month, and resigns.

events.text: {npc}, {ot_title}, has been found in {his} study, with a cord and a very respectful letter of resignation to Your Majesty. The letter is in a good hand, and it is not {his}. {He} had been {ot_child}'s since the spring. The Capital Guard reports no signs of anything. {ot_foe} has proposed a suitable successor, and sent a set of mourning robes that had been ordered some time ago.

choices.text: Have the letter read out, and compare the hand in open court

effects.log: It takes the clerks all morning. The whole court watches. {ot_foe} has a very bad hour, and {npc} gets a very good funeral.

choices.text: Accept the resignation, as written

effects.log: You grant {him} a posthumous title. The court has now learned what your silence will cover, and a good many people have started writing their wills.

events.text: {npc}, Minister of War, stands very straight. {He} wants a campaign, and the credit for it. There has been peace on the northern border for eleven years, {he} says, as if that were a charge. Both of your heirs have offered {him} a war, when the time comes. {He} would prefer to have one now, from the one person who can actually declare it.

choices.text: Give {him} a small war, on the northern border

effects.log: It is a splendid little war. The provinces pay for it. {He} comes home with a triumph, and your name is on it next to {his}.

choices.text: Play out the northern campaign with {him} on the map table

ok.log: You take {his} left flank on the second night, and {he} laughs out loud. Nobody has laughed in that room for years. {He} leaves the room yours.

fail.log: {He} takes your capital in three moves, and is extremely tactful about it.

choices.text: Remind {him} that peace is the point

effects.log: {He} agrees, wholeheartedly. {He} then goes to see how {ot_child} is keeping.

events.text: {npc}, Chief Censor, wants to read every memorial first. {He} says it would be a great saving of Your Majesty's time. {He} has been an honest official for forty years, and has impeached everyone at least once, including you. Both your heirs have offered {him} this already, once they are on the throne. {He} says {he} does not trust either one of them, and {he} would like to know if {he} can trust you.

choices.text: Grant it, and let {him} read yours too

effects.log: {He} takes a long breath. Your own memorials now go across {his} desk first, and {he} corrects your grammar. {He} would die for you, and {he} will tell you when you are wrong.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} would impeach you for today

effects.log: {He} has it with {him}, in {his} sleeve. It runs to three pages. You read all of it, and you make two changes. You are probably the first who ever has.

choices.text: Tell {him} the memorials come to you

effects.log: {He} bows. {He} has heard that from three Emperors. Your next impeachment arrives in a week.

events.text: {npc}, Minister of Revenue, wants an audit that never quite arrives. {He} has been very useful to you, and {he} is here to remind you of how much. {He} has also made some small loans to both of your heirs. The accounts of the empire are, {he} assures you, in excellent order, and they would be very hard for anyone else to read.

choices.text: Fund {his} retirement, and keep {him} on

effects.log: It is more than {he} stole, which is the point. {He} looks almost insulted, and {he} has been honest with you since, in the ways that matter. (-800 taels)

choices.text: Bring in your own auditor, from the salt tax

ok.log: The auditor finds it all in a week. You show it to {him} and you put it in a drawer. {He} has never worked so hard for anyone.

fail.log: The auditor finds a clean set of books, and then gets a better job. Somebody has been thinking ahead.

choices.text: Tell {him} you will have to think about it

effects.log: {He} is very understanding. The grain ships arrive late that year, and only those going to your side of things.

events.text: {npc}, Minister of Rites, wants a succession done by the old forms, and no other way. That means the eldest. Or if not the eldest, then the proper observances, a three-year consideration, an announcement to the ancestors, and {him} to be consulted at every stage. {He} has read everything, and {he} is the only person at court who is simply and truly horrified by what is happening.

choices.text: Debate the forms with {him}, for three days, from the classics

ok.log: You find {him} a precedent from the Second Dynasty that {he} had forgotten, and {he} weeps with joy. {He} would follow you anywhere, provided it was done correctly.

fail.log: {He} takes you apart, citing chapter and verse, and {he} is very kind about it. Half of the court comes to listen.

choices.text: Announce the three-year consideration, and put {him} in charge of it

effects.log: It is the happiest day of {his} life. Nothing can happen in that three years without {him}, and {he} is entirely yours. Your heirs both start to study the classics.

choices.text: Tell {him} Heaven's Mandate does not need a form

effects.log: {He} goes grey and does not reply. Next morning there is a very quiet memorial, on the subject of what Heaven does to those who say that.

events.text: The edict has been read, and {ot_foe} is Heir, and {ot_child} has been made a Prince of the first rank, with a beautiful palace, and nothing to do. {ot_He} has thanked you very correctly, three times. Since then a good many officials who were dismissed have turned out to have been {ot_his} friends. They have begun to hold poetry parties at {ot_his} new palace. The poems are about autumn.

choices.text: Invite {ot_him} to the palace and ask what {ot_he} would like

effects.log: It takes a long dinner. {ot_He} asks at last for the Western Marches, with an army, a long way from here. It is a risk. You give it to {ot_him}.

choices.text: Send {ot_him} to a very far province, with an honourable title

effects.log: The edict is beautifully worded. {ot_He} leaves within the week, and the poems become better known, and less about autumn.

choices.text: Have the poetry looked at, by the Censorate

effects.log: They find several disrespectful plum trees. It does no harm yet. {ot_foe} is not sure how to take it, and neither is {ot_child}.

events.text: The old sovereign left no edict. The Grand Council has searched every box, and they have all gone slightly grey. You are at the palace, in mourning white, and there is a crown in the room behind you. But {ot_foe} has reached the Northern Army first, and sends a respectful letter: {ot_fhe} is coming to pay {ot_fhis} respects at the funeral, with sixty thousand men.

choices.text: Hold the funeral at once, and be crowned at the graveside

effects.log: It is done in the rain, by the only three officials you can find. It counts. You will spend the rest of the war explaining why.

choices.text: Write back, and invite {ot_fhim} to come with an escort of one hundred

effects.log: It is a very proper letter. {ot_fHe} has it published. In the south, people have started to say you are a reasonable person, and they say it quietly.

events.text: There are six great provinces, and they are waiting to see. The ministers who were with you are arriving, and they have brought their families with them. You could spend this year in the capital with the seals and the Treasury and the old forms, and make it legal. Or you could go out and be seen by the armies of the south, before someone else tells them what you look like.

choices.text: Keep the capital, and rule

ok.log: The grain moves, the pay arrives and the courts sit. People who had been waiting to see begin to pay their taxes, which is the most honest thing a province ever does.

fail.log: The grain does not move. Someone has already been to see the Grand Canal. You are ruling a very handsome city, and not much else.

choices.text: Ride south and be seen

effects.log: You ride until you are hoarse. They have never seen one of the blood sit down on a camp stool. Some of them will remember that.

events.text: They have reached the capital. {ot_foe}'s vanguard holds the outer city, and the Palace Guard is holding the inner gates, for now. In the audience hall the ministers keep very busy burning things. Someone needs to go up on the wall of the Noon Gate. If it is you they will see it from the far side of the city, and if it goes badly they will see that too.

choices.text: Go up on the wall

ok.log: You stand on the Noon Gate, under the banner, in plain sight, through three assaults. Your arm is in a sling by evening, and the outer city has started to cheer for you.

fail.log: They bring you down off the wall on a door. The banner stays up, thanks to somebody you never see again. The inner gates have begun to be negotiated.

choices.text: Stay at the centre, and direct it from the tower

effects.log: You are a very good general, and it is a very long day. It holds. People will say you did not go up on the wall.

events.text: In the end the armies have stopped, as armies do, and the two of you have agreed to meet in the courtyard of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, with only the great officials to watch. Neither of you has a blade you are not entitled to. It is against every form there is, and the Minister of Rites has found a precedent. The one who walks up the steps is Emperor. The other gives up everything held.

choices.text: Draw

ok.log: You had forgotten how well {ot_fhe} fights. It costs you a good deal. Then you are on the steps, and the great officials are on the ground, all at once, like wheat.

fail.log: The sword is at your throat, and it does not move. You see the ministers go down on their faces, and you have just enough time to notice it is not to you.

choices.text: Offer a joint decree: the throne for one, and half the empire's armies for the other

ok.log: The Rites Ministry will need a decade to find a word for it. {ot_foe} looks at the paper, and at the armies, and at the sky, and signs on the lower line.

fail.log: {ot_fHe} reads it out to the officials, in a level voice, with your seal on it. Now the south has heard it as well. It will have to be next year, and on worse ground.

choices.text: Lay the crown on the steps, and walk away from it

effects.log: You set it down. Nobody knows what to do. It is {ot_foe}, finally, who picks it up, and {ot_fhe} does not look at you.

events.text: {ot_foe} is alive and in your hands, and is in a room with a good lock. Every Emperor who ever stood where you are has been advised the same way, by excellent people who loved the realm. Here is the Grand Councillor now, with a small cup on a tray. He says nothing. He only sets it down, where you can see it, and steps back.

choices.text: Make {ot_foe} a prince, and keep {ot_fhim} at court, where you can see {ot_fhim}

effects.log: It is held to be either very wise or very foolish, and it will be decades before anyone can tell. {ot_fHe} attends the audiences, in the third row.

choices.text: Send {ot_fhim} to a temple, very far away

effects.log: It is a very comfortable temple. There are a great many guards in it. {ot_fHe} sends you a letter at New Year, always on the same subject.

choices.text: Nod to the Grand Councillor

effects.log: He takes the tray away himself. There is a very fine state funeral, and you weep at it, in front of everyone, and nobody at all can tell.

events.text: {ot_foe} is on the throne now. The edict has given you a title, and a very fine residence, and it has also given you a day to reply. Your friends have stopped calling. There is an old custom by which someone in your position goes up and kowtows first, before anybody else. There is also a small door in the west wall of the palace that you learned about when you were nine.

choices.text: Go up and kowtow, first of all

effects.log: You touch your head to the floor nine times. {ot_fHe} says 'Rise' and you do. There will be a seat for you, and a very careful life in it.

choices.text: Take the west door tonight

effects.log: You have a good horse, and a letter of credit under some other name. The capital goes dark behind you, and you find, a good way down the road, that you can breathe.

events.text: You hold high office, or a high command, and so you have been invited to dinner. {ot_child}, of the imperial blood, keeps an excellent cook, and would value your opinion on a small matter of the succession. The next evening {ot_foe}, also of the imperial blood, keeps an even better one. Between the two dinners, somebody has gone through your desk with great care, and has tidied it.

choices.text: Send {ot_child} a very warm note

effects.log: It is a very warm note. It will be read in time by a surprising number of people, and you have signed it.

choices.text: Send {ot_foe} a very warm note

effects.log: It is a very warm note. Somebody writes back within the hour, and you can feel the whole court shift by an inch.

choices.text: Have a cold, for as long as it takes

effects.log: It turns out to be a very long cold. You are the healthiest invalid in the capital, and you have never been so closely watched.

events.text: The Son of Heaven is said to be resting. The palace gates shut an hour early, and an officer you do not know has come to your door with a request from your chosen prince. You and the seal of your office are wanted at the Noon Gate tonight. Nobody has said what for. By morning, one of two lists will be read out, and you will be on one of them.

choices.text: Go, with the seal, and everyone who will come

effects.log: You take every clerk, guard and cousin. Nobody could say that you held anything back, and that is very much the point.

choices.text: Send the seal, with your apologies. Your cold is worse

effects.log: The officer looks at the seal, and at you. It may be enough. It is the kind of thing that gets remembered both ways.

events.text: The elders have started pouring tea for {ot_child} and {ot_foe} before they pour for each other. It is a small thing. Over the winter the younger disciples have begun to stand in two groups at the morning forms, and nobody told them to. Somebody has asked you, very respectfully, who will lead the spring ceremony if you should happen to be in seclusion. You have not said anything about seclusion.

choices.text: Have everyone drill in a single line, you at the head

effects.log: They drill. The line has a very slight bend in it, around the middle, and everyone in it could tell you why.

choices.text: Say you may go into seclusion, and see what happens

effects.log: You do not go. But by the end of the week you know who has been thinking about the keys to the Scripture Hall.

events.text: A visiting elder from another sect has asked, over wine and in the friendliest way, whether it is true that the leader's seat will go to {ot_child}, or was it {ot_foe}? He has heard it both ways. So has everyone else, it appears. In the training yard your two heirs still bow to each other, a little more deeply each month, like two people measuring something.

choices.text: Say it will go to whoever is ready, when you are finished with it

effects.log: It is an excellent answer, and he goes away and repeats it. Everyone hears that there is a race.

choices.text: Set them to run the disciples' tournament together

effects.log: It is well run. The results have an odd pattern, and each of them is now very familiar with the other's best students.

events.text: {ot_child} likes teaching the youngest ones their stances, and would be happy doing it until {ot_he} is ninety. But the Elder of Discipline has started sending the promising ones to {ot_him}, and the Elder of the Stores has found {ot_him} a larger room. Nobody has asked {ot_him} anything. They have merely begun to refer to '{ot_child}'s people', and {ot_he} is not sure when {ot_he} got any.

choices.text: Tell the elders to leave {ot_him} to teach

effects.log: They are very sorry for any misunderstanding. {ot_child} looks at you with such relief that you can hardly stand it. It holds for a while.

choices.text: Tell {ot_him} a leader of people teaches too

effects.log: {ot_He} takes it as you meant it. {ot_He} is very good. You do not see {ot_him} with the small ones much any more.

events.text: {ot_child}'s disciples have beaten {ot_foe}'s at the spring trial, by a single point, on a judge's decision. It has now been three weeks, and nobody will drop it. A broken practice sword has been found in somebody's bedding. Younger disciples have started refusing to share a table. All of this is over a trial whose prize is a good wooden staff.

choices.text: Hold the trial again, and judge it yourself

effects.log: {ot_foe}'s side wins by a point. Now nobody is speaking to you, either, and they are all practising very hard.

choices.text: Give the staff to the disciple who fetched the water

effects.log: It is the only thing they have all agreed about for months: that it was outrageous.

events.text: {ot_foe} has gone off and defeated a notorious bandit, alone, in three moves, and the sect's name is on every tongue in the province. {ot_child} has stayed at home and cleared the old debts with the town, and the rice merchants have started sending the sect their best. You have to admit both of these are exactly what you would want in a leader. They are also both, very clearly, addressed to you.

choices.text: Praise neither, and set them both to sweep the courtyard

effects.log: They sweep it side by side, for a month, in full view. They are both very good at it. There is a certain amount of leaf-based hostility.

choices.text: Have {ot_foe}'s victory entered in the sect's annals

effects.log: It goes in with a fine flourish. {ot_child} goes to the archive to read it, and to count how many lines it got.

events.text: The Scripture Hall reports that the sect's third-level manual has been signed out, a great many times, by both of your heirs, and that each has been reading what the other has been reading. They have both advanced remarkably. It is an odd way to come by a great cultivator, let alone two. You find you are a little afraid of what it means that they are both so good.

choices.text: Teach them the fourth level, together, in person

effects.log: They learn it very fast, in a very uneasy silence. It may be the last thing the three of you ever do in one room.

choices.text: Close the third level to everyone for a year

effects.log: The disciples complain. Your heirs do not. They already have it, and they have both made copies.

events.text: The Stores are short, by a great many pills. The Elder of the Stores is horrified and has brought you the book, which shows that they were signed out to {ot_child}'s disciples. It is {ot_his} seal. {ot_child} says that {ot_his} seal has been in a box, and that the box has been in a room. {ot_foe} has offered, with real sympathy, to help look into it.

choices.text: Check when the seal was last cut

ok.log: It is a copy, a very good one, and the man who cut it has recently come into some rice land. It belongs to a cousin of a friend of {ot_foe}'s. You thank {ot_foe} for {ot_fhis} kind offer of help.

fail.log: It looks like {ot_his} seal. It really does. The disciples look at {ot_him} sideways at dinner.

choices.text: Replace the pills yourself, and say the count was wrong

effects.log: Nobody believes it, though they are all obliged to say so. {ot_child} owes you, and so does whoever did it. (-400 taels)

events.text: A letter has come from another sect, thanking {ot_foe} for a demonstration of certain forms. It is a very cordial letter. Those forms are not meant to leave the mountain, and if the letter is true, it is a matter for the Hall of Discipline. It was opened by mistake, by the one person guaranteed to read it aloud, and it has reached you only after it reached everybody.

choices.text: Write to the other sect yourself, and ask them straight

effects.log: They reply they have no idea what you mean. They also send it on to five other sects. It is a very strange sort of honesty, and the rumour dies.

choices.text: Send {ot_foe} before the Hall of Discipline, as anyone else

effects.log: It is correct. {ot_fHe} is cleared, after a full year of being watched. {ot_fHe} comes out thinner, and quieter, and much more dangerous.

events.text: Three disciples have been found to have been writing down what is said at {ot_foe}'s table, and handing it in somewhere. They are all very young, and they cry. They do not know who it is for; it goes under a stone by the old well. You have them taken off that duty. The next week, your own attendant turns out to have been reading your correspondence for the same stone.

choices.text: Leave something under the stone yourself

effects.log: You leave a short letter, unsigned, to whoever comes. It says you know about the well. Nothing comes back. But after that the well stops being used.

choices.text: Set a watch on the well

effects.log: It takes four nights. The person who comes is one of {ot_child}'s, and they are very surprised. You now have a good idea how far it goes.

events.text: {ot_child} went down in the practice ring today, from a blow that should not have reached {ot_him}, by a junior who has no idea what happened. A meridian has been nudged. It would take a very skilled hand, and a very close one, to arrange that at breakfast. {ot_He} will recover. In a month. The junior has been crying for an hour, and the whole sect has been very polite to {ot_foe}.

choices.text: Have everyone's food checked from now on

effects.log: It is a very unpleasant thing to bring into a sect. The elders nod in silence. It is quieter now, and nobody eats with their friends.

choices.text: Treat {ot_child} yourself, for the whole month

effects.log: You do it in your own rooms. {ot_He} mends well, and now the whole sect knows where the leader's hands have been.

events.text: On the cliff road below the back mountain, a rope that {ot_foe} uses every morning has parted. {ot_fHe} caught the ledge with one hand, and it was a very good catch, and one of the best things you have ever heard of {ot_fhim}. The rope has been brought to you. It was not cut, exactly. It was rubbed with something over a number of weeks, by someone in no hurry.

choices.text: Find out who has been up on the back mountain

effects.log: The sect's books have a very convenient gap. Somebody at the gate does remember one thing, however, and you begin to look at {ot_child}'s rooms in a different way.

choices.text: Hang the rope up in the main hall, and say nothing

effects.log: It hangs there, and everyone walks under it on their way to breakfast. Nobody touches it. It is a very eloquent rope.

events.text: It has come to swords in the main courtyard. Two groups of disciples, with some of the younger elders mixed in, over who had the right to use the east training ground. There are people bleeding on stones that have not had blood on them since the founding. The bell has been rung, and no one is listening. A great many of the children have been shut in the kitchen by the cook.

choices.text: Walk into the middle of it, and order them to kneel

ok.log: They kneel, row by row. You have them stay there until sundown, including the elders. Then you go and thank the cook.

fail.log: Some of them kneel. You have to put two of them on the ground yourself. You see whose people did not stop, and they see you counting.

choices.text: Stand on the steps and watch who wins

effects.log: It stops after an hour. You now know a lot about the sect, and the sect now knows a lot about you.

events.text: {ot_foe}'s people have the Scripture Hall, and they say it is to keep it safe. {ot_child}'s people have the gate and the Stores. Nobody has been killed yet. Everyone is being terribly polite. The sect next door has sent a gift, with a message asking if you require any assistance. Their scouts have been on the road since the day before they could have heard.

choices.text: Order both groups out, on pain of expulsion

effects.log: They come out. A few of them hand in their robes rather than do so. It is the first time you have ever seen the yard look that empty.

choices.text: Send your own disciples to take back the gate, for {ot_foe}

effects.log: You now have a side, officially, and so does the sect. The gift from next door is returned, and it is not the last of those.

events.text: The elders have asked for a formal meeting, the kind with minutes. They are all there, and they have on their best robes, and the oldest one has brought the founder's sword from the hall and has laid it down on the table between you. They say nothing about it. {ot_child} stands first among them now, and {ot_foe} a little behind. The sword is pointing at nobody. It is waiting for you to say something.

choices.text: Hand the sword to {ot_child}, before them all

effects.log: {ot_He} takes it in both hands. The elders stand. {ot_foe} stands as well, as the rule demands, and you do not envy {ot_fhim} that moment.

choices.text: Expel {ot_foe}, and read the charge yourself

effects.log: It is the worst day the sect has had in a generation. You read it out in a steady voice, and {ot_fhe} takes off the robe and folds it, neatly, on the step.

choices.text: Put the sword back. Let them do as they will

effects.log: The next spring {ot_foe} walks out of the gate with a third of the disciples, and they found a new sect two valleys away. Now you have a neighbour.

events.text: {npc}, {ot_title} of {ot_hall}, has stood up in the elders' meeting and said in so many words that {ot_child} has the makings. There is a short silence, in which you can hear a good many people revising their plans. {He} says {he} will give {his} support to whoever understands what {he} wants, which is {ot_want}. {He} has been quite clear about it.

choices.text: Thank {him} for being frank

effects.log: {He} looks at you very steadily. That is one elder who is not going to be changing sides without saying so, at least.

choices.text: Fund {his} hall's new wing, and ask {him} to wait

effects.log: {He} is too old to be fooled, and too old to refuse the wing. {He} finds {he} has spoken a little too soon, and will not say more. (-300 taels)

events.text: Your listeners inform you that {npc} of {ot_hall} has been in a very good mood. A rare ginseng has been turning up in {his} rooms. Someone is paying off the debts of {his} family in the village. It leads back to {ot_child}'s outer accounts, and {npc}, who has lived on sect rations for forty years, is finding out what it is like to have a little something put by.

choices.text: Double whatever {he} was offered

effects.log: {He} takes it, with some shame. {He} is not much of a traitor and not much of an elder any more, but {he} is nobody's now. (-400 taels)

choices.text: Mention the ginseng, kindly, in passing

effects.log: You ask if it has helped {his} chest. {He} goes very red. You are fairly sure it is the first time {he} has ever done anything of the kind.

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} has a favourite student, who has been spending a good deal of time on the mountain paths with {ot_child}. It has now become official. There will be a wedding, and {npc} will stand for the bride's side, and the whole of {ot_hall} will be guests. The young people seem honestly happy about it. It is annoying how often that happens at just the right time.

choices.text: Give them your blessing, and mean as much of it as you can

effects.log: It is a fine wedding, with very good dumplings. Everyone can count the guests, and at least two of those at the wedding are in love.

choices.text: Send {npc}'s student on a long mission

effects.log: It is a very important mission, and very far away, and very well funded. Nobody says a word. The young one writes to {ot_child} every week. (-500 taels)

events.text: You have been watching the pattern of who gets which missions. {npc} of {ot_hall} has been {ot_foe}'s for years, as everyone knows. But for some time now, {ot_foe}'s disciples have been getting the bad roads, and {ot_child}'s the good ones, all done with a very fair-looking list. {ot_foe} has not noticed yet. Whoever talked {npc} round must be very persuasive indeed.

choices.text: Say nothing, and read the lists more closely

effects.log: You keep your counsel. It is a very peaceful thing, to know something like that and to go on drinking your tea.

choices.text: Move the lists to another elder

effects.log: You do it without comment. {npc} hands them over with a very blank face. {ot_child} has noticed, and {ot_he} is looking at you.

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} went up to the old cave for {his} yearly meditation, and did not come down. They found {him} sitting up, and it looks like a qi deviation, the physician says, without enthusiasm. {He} was the steadiest cultivator on the mountain, and {he} had come out for {ot_child} last spring. There is a little burned incense near the entrance, of a kind nobody here has any reason to use.

choices.text: Bring the incense before the whole sect

effects.log: You hold it up at the funeral. You name the shop in the town, and who has an account there. {ot_foe} has gone very pale. It does not bring {him} back.

choices.text: Enter it as a deviation, and bury {him} with honour

effects.log: It is a good funeral, and the sect mourns properly. All of the elders have started to meditate with someone else in the room.

events.text: {npc} of the Outer Court wants fighters who get to fight, and a say in who. {He} has been training up the outer disciples for thirty years, and {he} sees them handed around as chips by your heirs. {He} has come to you with a list of a hundred names and a very simple request, which is that nobody touches those people unless they ask {him}.

choices.text: Give {him} the list, signed: nobody but {him}

effects.log: It takes a bit of the sect out of your hands. {He} looks as if someone has given {him} back a limb. {His} hundred are yours by way of {him}.

choices.text: Go down and spar with the hundred, one after another

ok.log: It takes all day, and you get every name right. By evening they are shouting yours. {He} shakes {his} head and laughs, and {he} is with you.

fail.log: It is a lesson for everyone, including you. They are very respectful, and they help you up.

choices.text: Remind {him} who the disciples belong to

effects.log: {He} says of course, and goes back to the yard. The next time they are asked, they all belong to {him}.

events.text: {npc} of the Hall of Discipline wants to be the one who knows what everyone has done. {He} already very nearly is. {He} has brought you a box. It has in it a page on each of the sect's elders, and on both your heirs, and a blank page with your name on the top. {He} says {he} has never been able to fill it in, and that it worries {him}. {He} would like you to tell {him} what goes on it.

choices.text: Tell {him} the thing you are most ashamed of

effects.log: It takes an hour. {He} writes it down without changing {his} face, and blots it, and hands it to you to burn. Then {he} shows you the other pages. {He} is yours.

choices.text: Ask {him} what is on {his} own page

effects.log: {He} is silent for a very long time. Then {he} takes out a sheet from inside {his} robe, and lays it down on the table. It is not at all what you would have guessed. You have each other now.

choices.text: Take the box away from {him}

effects.log: You take it. {He} gives it up very easily. {He} has a copy, of course, and now you know {he} knows that you would.

events.text: {npc} of the Stores wants a free hand with the pills and the silver. {He} has been running the sect's accounts with a thoroughness that has made the sect solvent, and has made a good many enemies. Your heirs have both offered to get the rest of the elders off {his} back. {He} says that all this could be yours, and at a good price. The price is not high, considering.

choices.text: Pay, and sign the free hand

effects.log: {He} accepts it with a dry nod. The sect has never been richer, and you are never going to know how. (-800 taels)

choices.text: Go through the accounts with {him} and find {him} a better way

ok.log: You find a trick with the spring tax that {he} had missed. {He} stares at it, and at you, as if you had started speaking in tongues. {He} says {he} wishes you had come down years ago.

fail.log: You find nothing that {he} did not find first. {He} is very gracious about the time you wasted.

choices.text: Tell {him} the elders are right to watch {him}

effects.log: {He} says that is very likely. Next spring there is a shortfall in your own rations, and it is quite correctly documented.

events.text: {npc} of the Scripture Hall wants the founding arts taught whole, to the right people. Your heirs have both been teaching shortcuts to their followers, and it has broken {his} heart. {He} has brought you the oldest copy of the manual, and asks you to read a single page and tell {him} what it means. {He} is very old. It may be the only test {he} has left to give.

choices.text: Read it, and answer honestly

ok.log: You read for a long time, and you tell {him} what you see. {He} closes {his} eyes, and a tear goes down the side of {his} nose. Nobody has read that page right in sixty years. {He} is yours.

fail.log: You say what you can. {He} pats your hand, very gently. {He} takes the book away.

choices.text: Forbid any shortcuts to be taught, by anyone

effects.log: It gets you shouted at by two groups of very angry young people. {He} bows to the floor. Your heirs have lost something by it, and you have kept something.

choices.text: Tell {him} the sect has to fight with what it has

effects.log: {He} nods, and {he} is not surprised. {He} takes the old book back and locks it away, a little more carefully than before.

events.text: {ot_foe} has the sword now, and it was done properly. {ot_child} bowed with the others and has gone on teaching and training and turning up on time. Nobody can point to anything. But {ot_his} disciples stop talking when someone from {ot_foe}'s side enters a room, and the other day someone was heard to wonder, in the yard, how long the mountain will be able to hold two suns.

choices.text: Walk the back mountain with {ot_him}, and ask what {ot_he} wants

effects.log: You walk until your knees hurt. {ot_He} wants to found a branch hall, in the south, and take {ot_his} people there. It is the first you have heard {ot_him} say it. You agree.

choices.text: Send {ot_him} away on a mission with no end

effects.log: It is a very honourable mission. {ot_He} goes, and {ot_his} people look at you for a long time, and the yard becomes much quieter.

choices.text: Let the sword-holder handle it

effects.log: That is what the sword is for, you tell yourself, on most days. {ot_foe} has begun to look tired.

events.text: Your predecessor died with no name on the tablet. The elders have shut the gates to outsiders for the mourning. Now they stand in the yard with the sect's founder's sword on a table, and nobody is reaching for it. {ot_foe} steps forward and bows to it, in the correct way, and then turns and looks at you. The disciples have arranged themselves into two groups without anyone having said anything.

choices.text: Bow to it as well, and do not touch it

effects.log: It is well done. There is a sound in the yard like a breath going out, and you have just told them this can be done properly.

choices.text: Say that it should be settled now, in front of everyone

effects.log: It shocks some of them. Some of them liked it. {ot_foe} smiles, a little, and says that {ot_fhe} will be glad to, when the mourning ends.

events.text: The mourning gives you until the spring. Everyone in the sect is going to choose between now and then, from the elders down to the kitchen. You have some very good reasons for why it should be you. The disciples in the yard could be shown them, in person, one bout at a time. Or the elders could be told them quietly, one pot of tea at a time.

choices.text: Go round the elders, one pot of tea at a time

ok.log: You drink a lake of it. Most of them were waiting for someone to ask. By spring you have heard a great many old stories, and you know who will stand beside you.

fail.log: You drink a lake of it. They are very cordial. {ot_foe}'s people had already been there, and they had brought better tea.

choices.text: Go down to the yard, and spar with whoever asks

effects.log: You come back bruised every night. By spring there are young ones who copy how you hold your shoulders. It is hard to explain what that is worth, and it is worth a good deal.

events.text: It has come to it at last. {ot_foe}'s side has shut the Scripture Hall against you, and they have blocked the bridge up to the main hall. They have said they will open up to the rightful leader. Your own people are ready. All you need to do is go across the bridge. It is narrow, it has no rail, and everyone on the mountain will be able to see who is first.

choices.text: Go across first

ok.log: You get over. It takes three of their best, and you put each of them down as gently as you can. The doors are open when you get there, and it is very quiet.

fail.log: You are back on your own side of the bridge, with your arm hanging. A very young disciple has gone to get a physician, and is crying, and it is mostly for you.

choices.text: Wait them out, and cut off the kitchens

effects.log: It takes a month, and nobody writes songs about it. They come out hungry, and you have lost nobody, and you have gained a certain reputation.

events.text: The elders have ruled that it is enough. The two of you will meet in the old ring, in front of the whole sect, with the founder's sword on its table. Whoever puts the other out of the ring takes it up. The one who loses leaves the seat and all it holds, and may stay or go as the new leader decides. You know how {ot_foe} moves, and {ot_fhe} knows how you do. You learned it in this same ring.

choices.text: Step into the ring

ok.log: It goes on longer than any bout that has been fought here. At last {ot_fhe} is on the far side of the line, on one knee, and you reach for the sword and find that you can barely close your hand.

fail.log: You see the line go by. It is a very odd feeling, being out of a ring you have stood in all your life. {ot_foe} goes to the table. Nobody is cheering. {ot_fHe} does not look at you.

choices.text: Offer {ot_fhim} the first elder's chair and a free hand, for the seat

ok.log: You talk it out in the middle of the ring, with the whole sect straining to listen. {ot_fHe} looks at you for a long while. Then {ot_fhe} bows, to you, and it is over.

fail.log: {ot_fHe} shakes {ot_fhis} head, loud enough for everyone. It will have to wait another year, and you have told them all that you did not want to fight.

choices.text: Bow to {ot_foe}, and step back out of the ring

effects.log: You step over the line yourself, before the first blow. There is no sound at all. It may be the bravest thing anyone has done here, or the other thing. You will never be told which.

events.text: The sword is in your hand. {ot_foe} is alive, and {ot_fhe} is waiting for you at the edge of the ring, and so is the sect, to learn what kind of leader you are going to be. The Elder of Discipline has the rule-book open. The rules let you expel {ot_fhim}, or worse. The disciples {ot_fhe} trained are all looking at you.

choices.text: Raise {ot_foe} up, and make {ot_fhim} first among the elders

effects.log: You help {ot_fhim} to {ot_fhis} feet. {ot_fHe} looks at your hand for some time before {ot_fhe} takes it. It is a good beginning, or a very long trap.

choices.text: Expel {ot_fhim}, with honour

effects.log: You read it in a clear voice. {ot_fHe} takes off {ot_fhis} robe and folds it. A good many go down the mountain with {ot_fhim} over the next few weeks.

choices.text: The rule-book, to the last line

effects.log: You read it to the end. Nobody on that mountain ever speaks of that day in front of you. There are still young ones who cross the yard to avoid you.

events.text: {ot_foe} has the sword, and has done everything correctly. {ot_fHe} has asked you to come and see {ot_fhim} after the morning forms. It is a beautiful morning. You could go up and bow, and the elders would find a place for you, which would be a very decent place. Or there is the road down the mountain. You have seen it from up here all your life, and you have never once wondered where it goes.

choices.text: Go up, and bow

effects.log: You bow. {ot_fHe} gives you a chair among the elders, and it is well meant. You have the best view of the yard of anyone alive.

choices.text: Take the road down

effects.log: You leave your robe on the bed, folded. Nobody stops you. About halfway down, you start to wonder where it goes.

events.text: You are an elder of a sect you did not found, and {ot_child} and {ot_foe} would each like you to know how much they value your counsel. {ot_child} has sent over a very rare tea. {ot_foe} has offered to take over your most tiresome duties, so as to give you some rest. The one who sits above you has begun to forget names. The elders' meeting next month has a vote on it, and you have a vote.

choices.text: Drink {ot_child}'s tea, and thank {ot_him}

effects.log: It is very good tea. You will be expected to remember that, next month.

choices.text: Let {ot_foe} take over the duties

effects.log: They are taken over, with great competence. You now have a lot more free time, and a lot less idea what is going on.

choices.text: Return the tea, and keep the duties

effects.log: You stay very busy. They both look at you with a new sort of interest, and you are starting to feel your age.

events.text: The one above you did not come to the morning forms, and now the elders have been called to meet at an odd hour, with the doors shut. On the way you are met by your heir of choice, who has walked out in the rain to take your arm. There is to be a vote. Nobody is going to ask you directly. It is only that everyone is going to see where you sit.

choices.text: Sit at {ot_child}'s right hand, and speak first

effects.log: You speak first, and you speak well. It cannot be taken back now. You feel a good deal younger.

choices.text: Sit where you have always sat, and speak last

effects.log: You speak last. It is very dignified, and everyone can see exactly what it is.

events.text: At the New Year offering, the East Branch brought its gifts to {ot_child}'s door before it brought them to yours. It was explained afterwards as a matter of the road. The Steward of the Granaries has now begun sending the good rice to {ot_foe}'s table, as a matter of the harvest. Nobody says who will stand before the tablets after you. They keep not saying it, at length, over dinner.

choices.text: Seat them both beside you at the offering, in full view

effects.log: They sit, and everyone counts the dishes. There is the same number in front of each, and the servants have already been spoken to about it.

choices.text: Leave the seats as they are, and watch who moves

effects.log: Nobody moves, which is worse. By the Lantern Festival, everyone in the house knows which aunt is sitting where and why.

events.text: A very old aunt has died, and in sorting out her things they found a list of which of your line she thought should lead the house. It has been widely read. It says {ot_child} has the head and {ot_foe} has the spine, and that it is a pity they cannot be sewn together. Everyone thinks it is hilarious. Within a month you notice that the branch heads have started to quote it in support of one or the other.

choices.text: Have it burned, and hold the funeral again, properly

effects.log: It is burned. By then there are nine copies, and the aunt has become an authority. Nobody laughs about it now.

choices.text: Have it framed in the ancestral hall

effects.log: It looks very well. You have made a joke of it, or else you have made it law. People come to read it on their way in.

events.text: {ot_child} wants to run the family's orchard, and to be left alone with {ot_his} pears. But the River Branch has an old claim against the main line and needs someone of the main line to back it, and {ot_foe} has refused. So they come by the orchard in small groups to admire the pears, and call {ot_him} 'the elder line's best hope.' {ot_He} has no idea what they mean.

choices.text: Go and tell the River Branch to leave the pears alone

effects.log: You say it to their faces. They apologise very nicely. {ot_child} sends you a basket of the best ones, and you eat them very slowly.

choices.text: Tell {ot_child} what they mean

effects.log: {ot_He} listens. {ot_He} goes very quiet, and looks at {ot_his} trees for a while. Then {ot_he} asks you who is managing the River Branch these days.

events.text: There is a marriage to be arranged for a young cousin, and it is a very good one. {ot_child} has found a match with a great family in the north. {ot_foe} has found one with the richest house in the south. Both are splendid, and both of them come with friends who would remember who arranged it. The cousin, who is seventeen, has been told not to worry about it.

choices.text: Ask the cousin

effects.log: Nobody has thought of this, and there is a very long silence. The cousin chooses someone else. Both your heirs are furious, and it is the best thing you have done all year.

choices.text: Take the southern match

effects.log: The silver arrives by barge. {ot_foe} is given all the credit, by people who are already thinking ahead.

events.text: Bandits burned a mill on the clan's land, and {ot_foe} rode out with the House Guard before you had finished breakfast. {ot_child} has spent the time since quietly finding out who sold the bandits their horses, and it turns out to be a neighbour. So now there is a feud to think about, and a triumph to be celebrated, and each one of them has a banquet planned. They are on the same day.

choices.text: Combine the banquets, and sit in the middle

effects.log: It is a very large banquet. You make a speech about mills. There are many toasts, and no one gets up to dance.

choices.text: Attend {ot_child}'s, and have the neighbour to dinner

effects.log: The neighbour pays. It is very quiet and profitable. The House Guard has noticed where you dined.

events.text: The ancestral hall's roof needs mending, and whoever pays for it will have their name on the beam for the next three hundred years. {ot_child} has offered. So has {ot_foe}. Each has now offered rather more than the roof costs. The carpenter has come to you, and he is enjoying himself very much. He would like to know if this will be a gold beam or a very large gold beam.

choices.text: Pay for it yourself, and put no name on it

effects.log: It is an ordinary beam, and it is very sound. A lot of people look up at it, and there is nothing on it to read.

choices.text: Let them both pay, and let the carpenter use both names

effects.log: The carpenter carves them at opposite ends. In a few centuries, some child will ask you why that beam is so very expensive.

events.text: The Steward of the Granaries has discovered that the grain tallies from {ot_child}'s estates have been short for three years. {ot_foe} has been very reluctant to bring it to your attention. Here are the papers. It is true the figures are short. It is also true that the same figures have been passing through the hands of a clerk who has lately been married to {ot_foe}'s wet-nurse's daughter.

choices.text: Walk the granaries, and count the sacks yourself

ok.log: It is all there, to the last sack, though it is not in the place that the paper says. You send the tally back to {ot_foe}, with your compliments.

fail.log: The sacks are not there. They may never have been there. {ot_child} swears to it, and the whole house has heard.

choices.text: Make up the shortfall, and dismiss the clerk

effects.log: It is cheaper than finding out. {ot_child} is grateful, and {ot_foe} sends a fine gift to the clerk, on his way out. (-400 taels)

events.text: A woman has turned up at the gate, with a small boy, and a letter in {ot_foe}'s hand from fifteen years ago. She does not ask for anything. She simply stands there, in plain view, in the rain, until a very large number of your relatives have seen her. {ot_foe} says that {ot_fhe} has never seen her before. The letter is an excellent likeness. You notice that the boy does not look at all afraid.

choices.text: Bring them inside, and hear the whole thing, privately

effects.log: It takes an evening. She was paid to come, and she was promised more. You pay her a good deal more than that, and you keep the letter.

choices.text: Have them taken away quietly

effects.log: It is done quietly. The whole house knows about it within the hour, and nothing is ever going to be cleared up now.

events.text: It has been noticed that the old tablets have been moved. Only slightly. {ot_child}'s mother's line has been set just one finger's width above where it stood, on the second shelf, in the night. It would mean nothing to any stranger. To the branch heads it is like a cannon going off. The East Branch wants it put right immediately, and the River Branch would like to know who else's position is open for discussion.

choices.text: Put it back yourself, in front of them all

effects.log: You move it back one finger's width, with your own hands. It is the most-watched finger's width in the province. Nobody says who moved it.

choices.text: Have someone sleep in the hall from now on

effects.log: A very old servant takes up his blanket there. Nothing else moves. Whoever it was has stopped, and they know you know.

events.text: {ot_foe}'s horse threw {ot_fhim} on the bridge road, at a gallop, with something under its saddle-cloth. {ot_fHe} has broken a collarbone and will be fine. It is not the first accident of the season. The House Guard says it was a burr, and has brought you a burr, and it is a very clean burr. Everybody at dinner is talking about how well {ot_child} has been looking lately.

choices.text: Have the stables searched, and every groom questioned

effects.log: Two of them turn out to have new shoes. Neither knows anything of value. It is a good start, and the stable has become a very nervous place.

choices.text: Set your own man to saddle {ot_foe}'s horse

effects.log: There are no more accidents with horses. Everyone knows that you have done it, and they know what it says about what you believe.

events.text: A boat has gone over on the river with {ot_child} in it, on a calm day, at the one place where the current is bad. {ot_He} swam to shore. The boatman did not, and he had been hired that very morning. {ot_foe}, who hates the water, has lately been reading a very great deal about the river. {ot_child} sends word that {ot_he} is well, and that {ot_he} has taken up a great interest in boats.

choices.text: Send to find out where the boatman came from

effects.log: He comes from a village that is owned by the River Branch, and he had debts that were paid off the week before. You have an answer, and it leads to two more questions.

choices.text: Have them both to dinner, and serve river fish

effects.log: You watch them eat it. Nobody says anything about boats. It is an extremely good fish.

events.text: The house guards have drawn on each other in the ancestral courtyard. It began with a disputed gate at the East Branch's compound, and now it has come right up to the door of the tablets. Your aunts have shut themselves up in the women's hall and are throwing roof tiles at both sides. The neighbouring clan has sent a very concerned letter, and a man to count the casualties.

choices.text: Carry the first ancestor's tablet out, and walk into the courtyard with it

ok.log: Nobody on earth is going to fight across that. The swords go down. You stand there until your arms shake. An aunt throws one more tile, on general principles.

fail.log: They go still for a moment, and then someone at the back shouts something about the first ancestor's real heir. You have to carry it back in through the fighting.

choices.text: Bar the hall doors, and let them tire themselves out

effects.log: It goes on until dark. In the morning you settle the bills for the physicians, and now you can see very clearly who won.

events.text: {ot_child} has moved into the East Compound, with thirty armed cousins, for reasons of safety. {ot_foe} has taken the keys of the Granaries and the Treasury, for the same reasons. The cooks have divided. The family's tenants have been told by two different stewards to pay their rent to two different people, and are refusing, with great politeness, to pay either of them until somebody tells them who is going to win.

choices.text: Call a full council of the blood, and read out the family rule

effects.log: They all come, and they sit down in their proper order, and it takes three days. By the end, the keys are on the table. Nobody has forgiven anyone.

choices.text: Send the House Guard to help {ot_foe} clear the East Compound

effects.log: It takes an afternoon. It is the first time the guard has been used against the family in living memory, and you are the one who has done it.

events.text: They have come at last, all of them, the branch heads and the stewards and the very old cousins, to stand before you in the ancestral hall. The eldest of them points at the blank place on the second shelf, where an heir's name would go. He is holding a brush, and the ink is wet. He says the house will not last another winter like the last one. {ot_child} has the most behind {ot_him}, and {ot_foe} has nearly as much.

choices.text: Take the brush, and write {ot_child}

effects.log: You write it. The hall is very still. It is done before the ink has dried on the brush, and {ot_foe} is the first to bow, and you cannot read {ot_fhis} back.

choices.text: Strike {ot_foe} from the family register

effects.log: You have the register brought out, and you do it yourself. You know you are the only person who could. The hall is silent, and it stays that way for some time.

choices.text: Put the brush down

effects.log: They look at the brush, and then at you, and then go home. In the spring {ot_foe} moves out to the river country, with a third of the house, and has a new sign painted for the gate.

events.text: {npc}, {ot_title}, has come in person to wish {ot_child} a happy birthday, and {he} stayed for two days. For anyone who knows the family, that is the same as a signed treaty. {He} says that {ot_child} is the only one of your line who has really listened to what {he} wants, which is {ot_want}. Three cousins have already rewritten their invitations.

choices.text: Send your own good wishes to {him}

effects.log: You send them, and they are very cordial. It is a matter of public record now where {ot_hall} stands.

choices.text: Ask {him} to look after a little matter for you, with an advance

effects.log: It is a very large advance for a very little matter. {He} is suddenly much too busy to go to birthdays. (-300 taels)

events.text: It turns out that {npc}, {ot_title}, has been forgiven a very old debt by a lender in the provincial capital, and the lender has been repaid by someone. The trail is a short one: {ot_child}'s third-best steward did it, without much skill. {npc} has not actually done anything yet. {He} has only begun to agree with things that {ot_child} says, with a look of mild surprise.

choices.text: Buy the note back, and tear it up in front of {him}

effects.log: {He} watches the pieces go. Then {he} thanks you, a little sadly. {He} is free, for what that is worth, and {he} owes nobody. (-400 taels)

choices.text: Tell {ot_child}'s steward to practise

effects.log: The steward goes grey. By evening, {ot_child} knows that you know, and {npc} knows it too.

events.text: The matchmaker has been seen going between {ot_child}'s rooms and {ot_hall} with a very pleased expression. {npc}, {ot_title}, will be giving a daughter of {his} line. It is a very proper thing, given the families, and it will tie that whole part of the house to {ot_child} by blood, for as long as anyone is counting. The aunts have already begun to embroider.

choices.text: Give your consent, and a good gift

effects.log: It is the wedding of the year. {ot_foe} gets very drunk, in a controlled way, and starts asking about somebody's younger sister.

choices.text: Find an earlier promise that bars it

effects.log: An old betrothal turns up, in a fine old hand, and it is even partly genuine. The aunts stop embroidering. {npc} looks at you over the rim of {his} cup. (-500 taels)

events.text: You have been going through the accounts, and they say that {npc}, {ot_title}, has been {ot_foe}'s all along. But the good contracts of the last year have somehow all gone to {ot_child}'s people, and the bad ones to {ot_foe}'s. The figures are perfectly honest. It has been done by someone who knows {ot_foe} would never think to check, because the one who did it taught {ot_fhim} to read.

choices.text: Say nothing, and take notes

effects.log: It is very instructive. You come away with the distinct feeling you have been a little too relaxed about your own contracts.

choices.text: Hand the figures to {ot_foe}, as a family matter

effects.log: {ot_fHe} reads them twice. {ot_fHe} goes and visits {npc}, with a small gift. You do not hear what is said. Nobody does.

events.text: {npc}, {ot_title}, had a long and healthy life, and a very good dinner, and then {he} went to bed and did not wake up. {He} was {ot_child}'s, and had said so in public just last month. The family physician says that it was {his} age. The cat, which also ate some of it, says otherwise. {ot_foe} has already sent to the family to offer {his} widow a very generous pension.

choices.text: Have the cat buried with honours, and let everyone ask why

effects.log: They ask. You tell them, in front of {ot_foe}, at the funeral. It is a very pointed thing to do with a cat, and it works.

choices.text: Accept that it was {his} age

effects.log: It was a very good age, you say. Everyone agrees. The kitchen has started to taste things twice.

events.text: {npc}, Captain of the House Guard, wants an enemy, a budget and no interference. {He} has been guarding the clan's walls for twenty years from nobody. Your heirs have both been telling {him} that they have enemies in mind, and it has begun to dawn on {him} who the enemy would have to be. {He} has come to ask you very directly to give {him} something else to do before someone else does.

choices.text: Give {him} a budget and the river bandits

effects.log: They are real bandits, and {he} is very happy. The river is safer, and the guard looks outward, and {he} is yours. (-500 taels)

choices.text: Walk the walls with {him} and find the weak place {he} has missed

ok.log: You find it behind the old kitchens. {He} goes very quiet, and then says that nobody has looked at those walls in years, and it is a pleasure to work for someone who does.

fail.log: {He} shows you all of the weak places, and they are all very well in hand. It is a very pleasant walk.

choices.text: Tell {him} the walls are enough

effects.log: {He} salutes. {He} goes and looks at them for a while. Then {he} goes to see {ot_child}.

events.text: {npc}, Head of the East Branch, wants first news of every match the main line makes. {He} has married off forty-one relatives in forty years, and {he} considers it a kind of warfare. {He} has an excellent map of who is related to whom, which {he} unrolls on your table. Your heirs are on it, in two colours. {He} would very much like to put you on it, in your own colour, in exchange for a little news.

choices.text: Give {him} the news of the next three matches

effects.log: {He} rubs {his} hands together. It is a small price, and you can already feel the whole house being rearranged around you. {He} is yours.

choices.text: Ask {him} to draw you a match nobody would think of

effects.log: {He} is delighted. {He} has been wanting to do this one for years. It is outrageous, and it may even work, and {he} would walk through fire for you.

choices.text: Roll the map up, and hand it back

effects.log: {He} takes it without a word. There is a new colour on it by the morning, and it is not one that you would have picked.

events.text: {npc}, Steward of the Granaries, wants the keys, and nobody counting behind {him}. {He} has been keeping this family fed through four bad harvests and has not been thanked for it once. {He} has with {him} a bill, for forty years of being suspected, and it comes to a figure {he} has arrived at with care. Your heirs have both offered to pay it, when they are able to.

choices.text: Pay the bill, and hand over the keys

effects.log: {He} takes the money and looks at it. {He} says no one has ever just paid it. The family will eat, and you will never again know exactly how. (-800 taels)

choices.text: Thank {him}, properly, for each of the four harvests, by name

ok.log: You remember them all, and who starved elsewhere that year. {He} has to go and stand by the window for a while. {He} tears up the bill.

fail.log: You mix up the second and the third. {He} corrects you, and nods, and adds it to the bill.

choices.text: Tell {him} you will count whatever you like

effects.log: {He} bows. There is a shortage of the good rice, all that next year, on your table only.

events.text: {npc}, Head of the River Branch, wants {his} old claim admitted out loud: that the River Branch is the elder line, and has been for two hundred years. It has been a family joke for most of that time, and {he} does not think it is funny. {He} has brought you the original register, in a box. It takes you some time to see that {he} might be right, and that {he} is well aware of what that would mean for you.

choices.text: Read the register, and find a way to honour it that costs nothing

ok.log: There is a title for it, unused since the fourth generation: Elder of the First Line. It gives nothing, and it says everything. {He} weeps. {He} is yours, and so is all of the River Branch.

fail.log: The register says what {he} says it says. You cannot find a way round it. {He} watches you look, for a long time, and {he} takes it away.

choices.text: Admit it out loud, at the next offering

effects.log: You say it before all the tablets. The East Branch nearly dies of it. {He} kneels and it is the first time anyone there has seen {him} do so. It has cost you some standing.

choices.text: Have a good laugh about it, as everyone does

effects.log: You laugh. {He} waits politely until you have finished. {He} takes {his} box with {him}, and it goes to see {ot_child}.

events.text: The name on the second shelf is {ot_foe}'s. {ot_child} sent very beautiful flowers. {ot_He} has also taken over the management of the farthest estates, and {ot_he} has been an excellent manager, and the rents from those estates are arriving later every season, with very good explanations. At the last festival, you overheard {ot_his} children being told a story about how things used to be.
