choices.text: Go out to the estates and see {ot_him}

effects.log: It is a long ride, and {ot_he} shows you round. In the evening {ot_he} tells you {ot_he} wants the far estates as {ot_his} own, a branch of {ot_his} own. You sign it. It is the best bargain you ever made.

choices.text: Recall {ot_him}, and send {ot_him} away from the family's lands

effects.log: {ot_He} comes, and goes, and takes the rent-rolls with {ot_him} by mistake. There is a new sign up on a compound in the next province.

choices.text: Let it lie. The shelf is what counts

effects.log: The rents come later. The explanations get better. {ot_foe} has started visiting the far estates, in a very friendly way, with some of the guard.

events.text: The tablet is carved and standing with the others, and the blank place on the second shelf is the first thing anyone looks at. {ot_foe} has arrived for the mourning with forty cousins and a very respectful expression. The branch heads visit each other late at night. The house needs a head by the time the mourning ends. The brush is on the table.

choices.text: Take up the mourner's place at the front, and hold it

effects.log: You stand there for nine days. It is the head's place, and nobody has quite dared to say so yet. Your knees are never the same.

choices.text: Sit down with {ot_foe}, and share the tea of the mourning

effects.log: You drink it together. For a few minutes you are both children, and neither of you says anything about the brush. It may be the last time.

events.text: Everyone in the house has a price, and most of it is old. The East Branch wants a marriage. The stewards want to go on being stewards. You could go through the family register with the eldest aunts, finding out exactly who owes what to whom, back to the third generation. Or you could go out to the tenants and the far farms, who pay for all of it, and let them see your face.

choices.text: Sit down with the aunts and the register

ok.log: They feed you until you can barely stand. By the end you know all of it, including some things about your parent, and three branch heads get very polite letters.

fail.log: They feed you until you can barely stand. They tell you a good many things, and most of those are about you, and you do not enjoy any of them.

choices.text: Go out to the far farms

effects.log: You help with the harvest in one village, badly, and they laugh about it for years. Two estates decide they could pay their rent to you.

events.text: It is out in the open now. {ot_foe}'s cousins hold the East Compound, and the road to it, and they have sent word that the House Guard may enter when it has a head to take orders from. The gate is an old one. Your great-grandparent built it. Someone is going to have to walk up and knock, or do more than that, and all of your relatives are watching from the roofs.

choices.text: Walk up and knock

ok.log: They open up to you. It is not without some unpleasantness in the courtyard. You sit down at the East Branch's own table, and you ask them for some tea, and they bring it.

fail.log: The gate does not open, and those on the roof have a good view of how you leave. Your aunts send you some very strong soup.

choices.text: Buy up the debts of those inside, and wait

effects.log: It takes a season. Then the compound's rice runs out, and its lenders call. They come out one family at a time. Nobody will write any songs about it.

events.text: Everyone is tired of it now. The eldest cousins have ruled that it will be done in the old way: the two of you, before the tablets, in the courtyard swept clean. Whoever is left standing writes a name on the second shelf. The loser gives up everything that is held by the head, and it will be written down in the family register for as long as there is a family. Your aunts are all watching from the windows.

choices.text: Take off your outer robe

ok.log: It ends with {ot_foe} sitting on the swept stones, looking mildly surprised. You walk in to the tablets on legs that are hardly yours, and pick up the brush.

fail.log: You are sitting on the swept stones. {ot_foe} walks past you and goes in. You can hear the brush from here, or you think you can.

choices.text: Offer to split it: the seat for you, and the river lands and half the rents for {ot_fhim}

ok.log: It is very like the deal you could have had two years ago, for a lot less grief. {ot_fHe} looks at the windows, and at the aunts, and sighs, and agrees. The name on the shelf is yours.

fail.log: {ot_fHe} laughs, not unkindly. It will have to be next year. All of the aunts have heard that you asked.

choices.text: Walk in and write {ot_foe}'s name yourself

effects.log: Nobody has ever done that. You write it very well. You come out, and an aunt takes you by the arm, and she does not say anything at all.

events.text: Your name is on the shelf. {ot_foe} is alive, and in the guest rooms, with a guard at the door that the two of you used to climb out of. The family is waiting for you to say something. The eldest cousins remind you that there is a rule for this in the register. It has only been used once, and that branch of the family is not spoken of, and nobody now knows where they are buried.

choices.text: Give {ot_foe} the river lands, and invite {ot_fhim} to the New Year

effects.log: {ot_fHe} comes to the New Year. It is very awkward, and there is plenty of food. The next generation will grow up knowing one another, which is the whole point.

choices.text: Strike {ot_fhim} from the register, and send {ot_fhim} away

effects.log: It takes one stroke. {ot_fHe} leaves by the front gate, on {ot_fhis} own horse, and the servants stand out on the steps. Some of them are crying, and they do not hide it.

choices.text: Use the rule

effects.log: You use it. Nobody is going to speak of it. You have become the sort of person the family does not mention, and you are the head of the family.

events.text: {ot_foe}'s name is on the shelf. You have been very politely asked to dine, and everyone will be there. You will be seated quite high up, and every eye will be on how you use your chopsticks. The family has always been very good at this sort of thing. There is a pony in the back stable that nobody counts, and the river is not so far.

choices.text: Go in to dinner, and bow first

effects.log: You bow, and you sit, and you eat every dish, and you ask after everyone's children. It is the hardest fight you have ever been in. Nobody can say that you lost it.

choices.text: Take the pony

effects.log: You go at dusk, with one bag. Your oldest aunt is standing at the back gate, with some money wrapped up in a cloth, and she does not say a word.

events.text: You have standing in a great family, though you are not its head. So {ot_child} and {ot_foe} have found they have business in your part of the house. {ot_child} has remembered your birthday, for the first time in thirty years. {ot_foe} has brought over a very nice young person for your line. The head of the house has lately been asking the same question twice at dinner.

choices.text: Accept {ot_child}'s birthday wishes, warmly

effects.log: It is a very good gift. You have been counted. An aunt nods to you across the courtyard.

choices.text: Look over {ot_foe}'s young person

effects.log: The young person is charming. The contract is very long. You are going to be related to this for quite some time.

choices.text: Say you are too old to remember whose birthday it is

effects.log: They laugh. They do not believe you. Nobody is going to invite you anywhere for a while, and you get a great deal of reading done.

events.text: The head of the house has taken to bed. All the branches have been sent for, and they have arrived a bit too quickly. Your cousin has sent someone to see you to your seat, which turns out to be very near the door of the sickroom, on one particular side of the room. Everyone is going to be able to see it, and you still have time to find that your knee has been troubling you.

choices.text: Sit where you were put, and stay all night

effects.log: You sit, and you stay. By morning everyone has looked at you more than once. It is done, and your knee is indeed killing you.

choices.text: Send your regrets. It really is your knee

effects.log: It really is. You send a very fine gift. It is the sort of thing that will be counted later, both ways.

events.text: {ot_child} has been to see {npc} of {ot_hall}, and has come out rather faster than {ot_he} went in. {npc} wants {ot_want}, and says that {ot_child} has offered {him} everything except that. {He} has told the story at dinner, with gestures. {ot_foe} is said to have enjoyed it a great deal, and to be taking notes on what not to say.

choices.text: Let {him} know you enjoyed it too

effects.log: A small jar of something good goes across to {ot_hall}. Nobody can say what it means, and {npc} is very pleased.

choices.text: Let it pass

effects.log: You let it pass. {ot_child} tries again in the spring, with a better offer. {He} will have heard about that as well.

events.text: {npc} of {ot_hall} has sent {ot_child}'s gifts back, all of them, in the same boxes, with a list. It is an itemised list and very correct. At the bottom, in {his} own hand, is one line: that {he} has served {ot_seat} since before either of them was born, and does not intend to start serving anything smaller. You keep rereading that line.

choices.text: Send {him} a word of thanks

effects.log: It is a very short word. {He} is not yours, exactly, but you know who you would go to on a bad night.

choices.text: Ask {ot_child} what {ot_he} learned

effects.log: {ot_He} says that {ot_he} has learned the size of the boxes. You think {ot_he} is joking. You are not sure {ot_he} is.

events.text: They both went to {npc} on the same day, by accident or otherwise, and met on the stair. {npc} of {ot_hall} gave them each a cup of tea, in the same room, and talked for an hour about the weather, and sent them both away. {He} has said since that it was the most useful afternoon {he} has had in years. {ot_child} and {ot_foe} are both very angry, about slightly different things.

choices.text: Have {him} to tea yourself, and talk about the weather

effects.log: It is excellent weather. You both agree it may change. You think you have understood one another.

choices.text: Do nothing

effects.log: You do nothing. {He} goes on being the one person in the house who is not afraid of either of them. It will not last, and you know that.

events.text: You have given each of them something, on the same day, of very nearly the same size, and taken a little from {ot_child} so that it would come out even. It takes a clerk two days to work out the figures. Everybody knows just what you are doing. {ot_child} comes to thank you, and is very formal about it, and you can hear what {ot_he} is not saying from across the room.

choices.text: Tell {ot_him} {ot_he} is the reason you had to do it

effects.log: {ot_He} takes it as praise. It is, in part. It goes a little better than you deserve.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let it be an order

effects.log: {ot_He} bows, and goes. You have never felt so much like an abacus.

events.text: It is very quiet in the house this month, the kind of quiet you get when everybody has just been given exactly what they deserve and none of them likes it. {ot_foe} has sent you a note: {ot_fhe} would like to know how much further you expect to go on doing this, and whether there is a form {ot_fhe} might fill in. It is a very funny note. You are not sure {ot_fhe} meant it to be.

choices.text: Write back, as a joke, with the form

effects.log: You send it, filled in. {ot_fHe} frames it. You may have just had the first conversation with {ot_fhim} in years.

choices.text: Do not answer

effects.log: You do not answer. The quiet goes on for the rest of the year, which is as much as you ever really buy.

events.text: Your scale has been noticed from outside. A visitor has said, with some admiration, that you must be the best juggler in the murim, and asked how long your arms are going to last. {ot_child} and {ot_foe} are both at the table. They stop eating, and look at you with the very same expression, and for one moment you can see how much alike they are.

choices.text: Laugh, and pour the visitor another

effects.log: You all laugh. It is a very good evening, and nobody at the table has been fooled.

choices.text: Say that your arms will outlast the question

effects.log: It goes very quiet. One of them almost smiles. You have reminded them who is still in the room.

events.text: You have told {ot_child}, in strict confidence, that {ot_foe} is further ahead than {ot_he} thinks. You have told {ot_foe} the same about {ot_child}. The results have been remarkable. Tribute is up. The treasury has never been so full. Both of them have started arriving early to morning business, and neither of them has slept since the spring. You feel very well, and you are trying not to think about why.

choices.text: Enjoy it

effects.log: You enjoy it. It is the best year of your rule. You catch sight of yourself in a bronze mirror one day, and you do not stop to look.

choices.text: Ease off a little

effects.log: You let a few things drop. They have noticed, and they each decide it means the other one has got to you first.

events.text: {ot_foe} has brought you a gift, the sort of thing a person only gets by doing something unforgivable to someone else. {ot_fHe} is very pleased, and watching your face. Behind {ot_fhim} you can see {ot_child}, with a gift of {ot_his} own. You taught them both to do this. You did it so well that you are honestly not sure if they know they are doing it for you.

choices.text: Accept them both, with exactly equal pleasure

effects.log: You are very pleased, and you tell them so. They both go off happy. You have the gifts put somewhere you will not have to see them.

choices.text: Ask {ot_foe} what it cost the other person

effects.log: {ot_fHe} tells you, a little puzzled. It is exactly what you thought. {ot_fHe} goes off wondering what you wanted {ot_fhim} to say.

events.text: One of your old companions has come to see you, somebody who has known you since before all this. They sit with you for a long time and they do not say much. As they get up they say that you were kinder to your enemies than you are being to your own, and that they are too old to be afraid of you. You have them shown out with every honour. They have left their cup half full.

choices.text: Think about it

effects.log: You think about it, most of that night. Then you send a very small kindness to each of them. They are both deeply suspicious.

choices.text: Do not think about it

effects.log: You do not think about it. There is a great deal to do. You are very good at not thinking about it.

events.text: It came out over nothing: a posting, a date, a clerk who keeps very neat records. Someone sat down with five years of small decisions and laid them all out in a row, and they all fall the same way, toward {ot_child}. {ot_foe} has read it. {ot_fHe} has come to you and set it on your table, and {ot_fhe} does not shout. You have never heard {ot_fhim} speak so quietly.

choices.text: Tell {ot_fhim} the truth

effects.log: You tell {ot_fhim}. It is worse than a lie would have been, and it is the only thing you have given {ot_fhim} in years that was real.

choices.text: Deny it

effects.log: You deny it, very well. {ot_fHe} listens to the end. {ot_fHe} picks up the papers, and bows, and from now on {ot_fhe} will not believe you about the time of day.

events.text: Your favour has been read, as all things are in the end. The first you hear of it is {ot_foe}'s people, who have stopped asking you for anything. The second is {ot_child}, who comes to you white in the face to say that you have got {ot_him} killed. {ot_He} did not know. All these years, {ot_he} truly thought that {ot_he} was doing rather well.

choices.text: Tell {ot_him} {ot_he} did do well

effects.log: It is true, and it is no use to {ot_him} at all. {ot_He} goes away and starts checking everything {ot_he} ever won, from the beginning.

choices.text: Tell {ot_him} to get used to it

effects.log: {ot_He} stares at you. {ot_He} does. It is a very quick education, and you have paid for it, and so has {ot_he}.

events.text: A song is going round the lower halls about a cook who only ever salts one dish. It is very funny, and it has eleven verses. By the seventh it is clear who the dish is and who the cook is. {ot_foe}'s people sing it the loudest. {ot_child}, to {ot_his} credit, has learned all the words. You have started hearing it in your sleep.

choices.text: Have it stopped

effects.log: It stops, and so everyone knows it was true. The twelfth verse is about that.

choices.text: Hum along, where they can hear

effects.log: It takes the fun out of it for nearly everyone. It does not make anybody forgive you.

events.text: It took one afternoon. All that {ot_child} built in all those years has been taken down in front of everyone, and {ot_his} people have been sent to the far gates. {ot_He} keeps {ot_his} life and {ot_his} name, and not much else. {ot_He} did not plead. {ot_He} stood and watched it being done, and at the end {ot_he} thanked you, in the proper form, in a voice you will hear for a long time.

choices.text: Go to see {ot_him} that night

effects.log: You go. {ot_He} is sitting in the dark. Neither of you says very much. You could not tell anyone whether it made things better, but you went.

choices.text: Do not go

effects.log: You do not go. You are told that {ot_his} lamp burned all night. It is a very quiet house now, and they are all looking at the floor.

events.text: The house is very orderly since you broke {ot_child}. People are at their posts on time. Those who were {ot_his} have been very careful to tell you they never really were. {ot_foe} has become a model of good behaviour and of respect, and comes to see you every morning, to ask if there is anything else you would like done. You had thought {ot_fhe} would look happier.

choices.text: Ask {ot_foe} what {ot_fhe} is afraid of

effects.log: {ot_fHe} looks at you for a long moment, and then gives you a very correct answer. You did ask.

choices.text: Give {ot_foe} something to do, far away

effects.log: {ot_fHe} goes at once. Nobody has been this obedient to you since you took the seat, and it is not as pleasant as you had once imagined.

events.text: You have been told what they call it now, in the corridors: 'the afternoon.' As in, 'that was before the afternoon.' Young people who were not there use it. Somebody has been sending a small bowl of rice to {ot_child} every day, and nobody seems able to find out who. You have not tried very hard. You have started to wonder what you would have had to do to be forgiven.

choices.text: Add a little something to the bowl

effects.log: It goes on the tray with the rest. Nobody knows. It is the kind of thing you would have laughed at, once.

choices.text: Stop asking about it

effects.log: You stop asking. The rice goes on. So does everything else.

events.text: It is done. You have said the name, in front of everyone, and {ot_child} is your heir, and you did not know how much of your strength had been going into not saying it. People you have not seen smile in years are smiling. {ot_foe} has been the first to bow, in the proper form, and you look for a long time at the top of {ot_fhis} head.

choices.text: Go to {ot_foe} that evening, alone

effects.log: You do not have much to say to {ot_fhim}. You say it anyway. {ot_fHe} hears you out, and it helps a little, and you can tell that it does not help enough.

choices.text: Leave {ot_foe} to the new order of things

effects.log: There is plenty to be done. You see to it that {ot_child} starts learning what it weighs. It is very late before you think about the other one again.

events.text: They told you it would be a relief, and they were right. {ot_child} has moved {ot_his} things up to the Heir's rooms, and has asked you three very good questions about the accounts, and one bad one. You have started to sleep. In the morning someone comes to tell you that {ot_foe} has given a very fine dinner for those passed over, and that everybody there had a very good time.

choices.text: Send a dish to the dinner

effects.log: It is your own cook's best. They eat it. It is a way of saying that you know where they all are, and you mean that kindly.

choices.text: Ask for the guest list

effects.log: It is on your desk by noon, and it is longer than you would have liked. You put it where you will see it every day.

events.text: You named {ot_child} because you were tired, or because it was right. You are not sure that it makes much of a difference, and you never will be. Whatever {ot_foe} would have been is now going to be something else. You look at the two of them for a while across the hall, doing all the right things. It strikes you that this is the first time they have stood so far apart, and looked so much at ease.

choices.text: Tell {ot_child} to be good to {ot_foe}

effects.log: {ot_He} promises. You can tell {ot_he} means it. You have seen a good many people mean it.

choices.text: Tell {ot_child} to be careful of {ot_foe}

effects.log: {ot_He} nods. {ot_He} has already been very careful for years. You have just told {ot_him} that you meant {ot_him} to be.

events.text: There is only {ot_child} left, of all those who wanted it. You have looked for the moment when you decided this, and you cannot find it. You kept saying nothing, and the others died or went away or stopped asking, and now {ot_he} comes to morning business alone, and everyone bows to {ot_him}, and it has all been settled without you. {ot_He} has not asked you for anything.

choices.text: Name {ot_him}, then

effects.log: You name {ot_him}. Nobody is surprised. {ot_He} thanks you, and you find you cannot look {ot_him} in the eye for very long.

choices.text: Go on saying nothing

effects.log: You go on saying nothing. It does not seem to make much difference now. {ot_He} pours your tea very carefully.

events.text: A very old servant, who has been with you since the beginning, is sweeping the great hall. She looks up as you pass, and says that it has got a lot quieter around here. Then she goes back to her sweeping. {ot_child} is the only one of them who still lives here. There were more. You could give all of their names, and the years, and you find that you have stopped on the stairs to do it.

choices.text: Have {ot_child} to dinner, just the two of you

effects.log: It is a good dinner. Neither of you mentions anybody. You both eat a great deal, as people do after a funeral.

choices.text: Go on up the stairs

effects.log: You go on up. It is a lot of stairs. You have never noticed that before.

events.text: They bring you {ot_child} on a door. It was over nothing, they tell you: a stair, a bad moment, someone who may not have known who it was. {ot_foe} stands a long way off with {ot_fhis} hands open, looking as if {ot_fhe} might be sick. Somebody has closed {ot_his} eyes. You knew this could happen. You said so to yourself, and to nobody else.

choices.text: Find out who did it, and what you are going to do

effects.log: You find out. It does not take long, and it does not help. The person is very young. You sit up with what is left of the evening, and you do not come to any decision at all.

choices.text: Carry {ot_him} in yourself

effects.log: You send away the people with the door. It is a long way up to the hall. Nobody dares to help you, and nobody has ever seen your face like that.

events.text: A letter was found in {ot_child}'s coat, addressed to you, not finished. It says that {ot_he} has been meaning to ask you something for quite a long time. It does not say what. They fought all night in the halls, and in the morning {ot_he} was one of those who did not get up. The whole house has stopped fighting, for now. You keep on turning the letter over, as if there could be more on the back.

choices.text: Name no one, and shut the house for a year of mourning

effects.log: You shut every gate for a year. Nobody fights. Nobody speaks to you, either. They are all waiting to see if you have learned anything.

choices.text: Have the fighting stopped for good, whatever it takes

effects.log: You give the order. It is the order you could have given at any time in the last twenty years, and everyone knows it.

events.text: It has been some years since you named {ot_foe}, and {ot_child} has done nothing at all that anybody could object to. That is starting to be remarked on. {ot_His} old friends are doing rather well, in quiet posts, in a good many places. At the New Year {ot_he} sent {ot_foe} a very handsome set of tea bowls, and {ot_foe} has had them tested, and they are only tea bowls.

choices.text: Ask {ot_child} to come and drink from them, with both of you

effects.log: It is a very civil hour. Something eases, a little, somewhere around the second cup. {ot_He} asks after your health, and it seems that {ot_he} means it.

choices.text: Leave it

effects.log: You leave it. The bowls are put away on a high shelf, and {ot_foe} looks at them sometimes.

events.text: {ot_foe} has come to you about {ot_child}. {ot_fHe} has no proof of anything, {ot_fhe} says. {ot_fHe} would simply like to be told what you would do in {ot_fhis} place, and {ot_fhe} asks it the way you once asked someone the same question. You remember the answer you were given. You remember what you did about it, and you have never told anyone how it felt.

choices.text: Tell {ot_foe} to go and talk to {ot_child}, and mean it

effects.log: {ot_fHe} looks at you as if you had suggested flying. {ot_fHe} goes, in the end. You hear they talked until dark, and that nobody won.

choices.text: Tell {ot_fhim} what you did

effects.log: You tell {ot_fhim}, all of it. {ot_fHe} listens very carefully. Before the year is out {ot_child} has been sent a long way away, and you did that as well.

events.text: {ot_child} came to you this spring and asked for nothing. {ot_He} sat with you in the garden. {ot_He} said that {ot_he} used to lie awake working out how to beat {ot_foe}, and that lately {ot_he} has been lying awake trying to remember why. You wait for the rest of it. There is no rest of it. {ot_He} helps you up, when it gets cold, and goes in. You have no idea whether you have just been handled by a master.

choices.text: Believe {ot_him}

effects.log: You decide to believe {ot_him}, and you tell {ot_him} so. Whatever it was to begin with, it seems to have become true by the autumn.

choices.text: Have {ot_him} watched a little more closely

effects.log: You give the order, and you do not enjoy it. {ot_He} goes on coming to the garden. {ot_He} knows, of course.

events.text: You stepped down, and you gave the seat to {ot_foe}, and you thought that would be the end of it. {ot_child} has come to see you on the back mountain, with a basket of fruit and some questions about the old days. {ot_He} would like to know, as one who has always respected you, whether you think {ot_foe} is managing. {ot_He} sits with you for a very long time. {ot_He} has brought good fruit.

choices.text: Tell {ot_him} you have retired

effects.log: You say it pleasantly. {ot_He} agrees that you have. {ot_He} comes back next month, with more fruit.

choices.text: Tell {ot_him} what you really think of how {ot_foe} is doing

effects.log: You tell {ot_him}. It is a great pleasure. It will be repeated in the halls by nightfall, in your own words, as your considered view.

events.text: {ot_foe} sits your old seat, and has come up the path to ask your advice, very humbly. It seems that those who were {ot_child}'s have been slow in carrying out {ot_fhis} orders. Not refusing, only slow. They all say that they are waiting to hear what the old head thinks. {ot_fHe} looks very tired, and has started to look at you the way you once looked at your own predecessor.

choices.text: Go down, once, and stand behind {ot_foe} in the hall

effects.log: You stand there, for one morning. Nobody says a word. Their orders get carried out, for now. {ot_foe} has not thanked you, and you did not expect it.

choices.text: Tell {ot_fhim} that a seat holds itself, or it does not

effects.log: {ot_fHe} thanks you, and goes back down that long path by {ot_fhim}self. You watch {ot_fhim} for much longer than you meant to.

events.text: There has been a fight in the yard, down below, you are told. Someone took it on themselves to come up and tell you, and then someone else, with another story. Your hall on the back mountain is the busiest place in the house these days. You came up here to look at the clouds. You have not looked at any clouds at all this year, because there is a line of people at your door, and each has brought a small gift.

choices.text: Bar the gate and look at the clouds

effects.log: You have the path closed for a year. They are very good clouds. A lot goes wrong down there, and you can see some of it from here, and you do not go.

choices.text: See them all

effects.log: You see every one. Nobody can say you do not listen. You are running a second court, in a very small house, and {ot_foe} knows it.

events.text: {ot_sq}, who has been with you on your company's hardest roads, has started having dinner with {ot_child}. It is only friendship. {ot_child} remembers {ot_sq}'s children, and has found a very good post for a cousin. There is a word going round the company now, and it has to do with who will be keeping it when you are gone. {ot_foe} has started a little squad of {ot_fhis} own, and has borrowed your drillmaster.

choices.text: Ask {ot_sq} straight out

effects.log: {ot_sq} looks at you, and says the company is yours while you hold it, and then says nothing else. It is a very honest answer to the question you asked.

choices.text: Let it run. A soldier may eat

effects.log: You let it run. It is a small thing. It is also the first time you have looked at the roll and wondered.

events.text: A side needs swords of its own, it seems. {ot_child} has been giving the young officers of your company very good advice, and also very good horses. When you hold a muster now, you find that {ot_sq} and a few others have started to stand in a slightly different place. They would all die for you. They have only begun to consider what happens afterward, which is what you trained them to do.

choices.text: Move them apart at the next muster

effects.log: You do it as a matter of drill. They take the new places without a word, and you can feel the company looking at you.

choices.text: Give {ot_foe} a command in the company as well

effects.log: If there have to be two sides in it, at least it can be even. The company drills beautifully, in two halves.

events.text: A great house that you are tied to has sent a very friendly letter. It has noticed that the succession in your house has not been settled. Naturally it does not wish to interfere. It merely mentions that its younger daughter is of an age, and {ot_child} has made such a good impression, and that its people would be very happy to see {ot_him} doing well. You did know that the debt would come in some form.

choices.text: Thank them, and decline to hear what they did not say

effects.log: You write a very good letter. They write back a better one. They have not stopped sending presents to {ot_child}.

choices.text: Let them

effects.log: They have sent a very good many presents, and some people to go with them. There is now somebody else's banner, a small one, in your own courtyard.

events.text: It appears that the house you are tied to has been making {ot_child} some very reasonable loans. There are no conditions at all. It has only asked to be remembered, in due course. You have read the terms of your own tie again, and they say nothing about this. Nothing in them prevents a friend of the family from buying up the next generation of the family at a very good price.

choices.text: Buy the loans back

effects.log: It costs you more than you would like to admit, and you do it through a third party. They know. They send you a basket of fruit, with a card.

choices.text: Ask {ot_child} what {ot_he} thinks {ot_he} promised

effects.log: {ot_He} tells you, in some detail. {ot_He} has read all of it, and is rather further ahead on this than you are. It is somehow not as comforting as it ought to be.

events.text: The war needs generals, and the fronts are a long way off, where a person can win a name without anybody at home getting in the way. {ot_child} has asked for a front, and so has {ot_foe}. {ot_He} has offered to take the worst of them, in writing, and to pay for {ot_his} own supplies. People have noticed it is a very good way to come home with an army that owes you nothing but its life.

choices.text: Send {ot_child} to the front

effects.log: {ot_He} goes, and {ot_he} does well. {ot_His} letters home get shorter, and {ot_his} soldiers' songs have started to have {ot_his} name in them.

choices.text: Keep them both at home, under your eye

effects.log: They stay. It costs you a front, and a good general. They spend the time on each other.

events.text: You have conquered a great deal of the world, and it turns out that it has to be given to someone. {ot_foe} has been asking, with great respect, who will be governing what you took. {ot_child} has drawn up a map, in colours. The envoys from the regions you hold have started to bring two kinds of gift, and they are looking past you already, as a horse does when it knows the way home.

choices.text: Tell them that the world is still yours

effects.log: You remind them, at some length. They all bow. The map has been put away, somewhere very close at hand.

choices.text: Give {ot_foe} one region to govern, as a test

effects.log: {ot_fHe} governs it very well. In three years, it is the only part of your empire that does not ask you for anything.

events.text: You did not come by this seat gently, and now that people think of who comes after, it has started to come up. {ot_foe} has asked one of the old people, in a friendly way, what the custom is when a seat was taken by force. There are several customs. The kin of the one you took it from have remembered they are alive, and have sent a gift to each of your heirs.

choices.text: Have the old people to dinner, and ask about the customs

effects.log: You listen for an entire evening. It is a very instructive evening. Nobody leaves it thinking that you have forgotten how you got here.

choices.text: Remind them all how it was done

effects.log: You do not need to say much. You go and stand at the place where it happened, for a while, where everyone can see you. They are all very polite for a long time.

events.text: Someone who stood against you long ago has written to {ot_child}, full of praise and old stories. The house was once ruled another way, it says, and could be again. {ot_child} has brought the letter to you. You cannot tell what that means, and you can tell that {ot_he} knows you cannot.

choices.text: Thank {ot_him}, and burn it

effects.log: You burn it together. {ot_He} is very composed about it. You would have done just the same, at {ot_his} age.

choices.text: Ask {ot_him} how many others {ot_he} has not brought

effects.log: {ot_He} laughs, the first time you have ever heard it. {ot_He} says that that is a very good question. {ot_He} goes away without answering.

events.text: {ot_m} has taken to quoting you. {ot_m} holds the very post that you held on your way up, and it seems that your old notes are still there in the desk, and that they make very interesting reading to the young. {ot_child} has asked to see them, and so has {ot_foe}. Everybody now knows what you did to the person who held that post before you. You had rather hoped that was not in the notes.

choices.text: Have the notes brought to you, and read them again

effects.log: You sit up with them all night. You were very young, and very sure of yourself, and very good. You send them back, with a few corrections.

choices.text: Burn them

effects.log: They burn very well. {ot_m} has made a copy, of course. {ot_m} tells you so, with enormous respect, and you think that you might have got on rather well, in another life.

events.text: It is an odd thing to sit where you sit and watch someone else do your old job. {ot_m} is good at it. {ot_m} has made none of your mistakes, and several new ones. Both your heirs have been to call on {ot_m}, and it has been explained to them both, you are told, that the post is not what it once was, and that nobody who ever held it has ever really been loyal to anyone. You remember saying that. You remember who to.

choices.text: Go down and walk the old rounds with {ot_m}

effects.log: You walk them, and you know where each loose stone is. {ot_m} asks a very good question about the third stair. You come home in a better mood than you have been in for years.

choices.text: Leave {ot_m} to it

effects.log: You leave {ot_m} to it. It is what somebody should have done for you.

events.text: The report from your network is very thorough. It has a page on {ot_child} and a page on {ot_foe}, and the page on {ot_foe} has an appendix. There is a list of who has been paying whom, and it goes back rather further than you had thought. The handler wants to know if you would like them to go on. The handler also mentions that they have been approached, on behalf of one of your heirs, about reports on you.

choices.text: Have them go on, and take the approach

effects.log: Let them buy the reports. You will write them. It has been some time since you have enjoyed your work so much.

choices.text: Have them stop

effects.log: You burn it. It is what a decent person would do, and you have now told your best people that you do not want to know.

events.text: Your rivals in the trade have offered you a look at their file on your house, for a very fair price. They consider it a professional courtesy. It is very good work. They have {ot_child}'s side and {ot_foe}'s side, down to the kitchen staff. They have a small note in the margin, for their own people: that the head of the house knows less than anyone, and that this is what makes it such an interesting place.

choices.text: Buy the file

effects.log: You pay. You read it twice. It is the most unkind thing anyone has ever said to you, and it is all true. (-200 taels)

choices.text: Send it back with one correction in the margin

effects.log: You correct a date. They will spend a month working out what you meant by that, and you have spent nothing.

events.text: The jar is in its usual place. You know what it does. You have thought about how it would be, to have one of those four people across the table from you who cannot ever move against you, and how very quiet it would make the house. It would only take one cup of tea. Nobody would know, ever, apart from you and the thing in the jar. It has been very patient, and it has started to move about a bit in the evenings.

choices.text: Leave the lid on

effects.log: You leave it on, this year. It does not mean anything. You have only said to yourself that you could.

choices.text: Take it down, and look at it for a while

effects.log: You have it on the table all evening. You know now which one of them you would pick. (A worm can be set from the same place as the rest of this.)

events.text: Someone has been asking the herb-sellers about a very particular kind of worm. It is not you. You have your own. It would seem that one or the other of your heirs has been thinking along the same lines, and you have to admit that it is exactly what you would have done. You look at your own people over dinner, and you notice how carefully each of them is eating.

choices.text: Have the herb-sellers bought out

effects.log: You buy every jar in three provinces. It is an expensive way of saying that you noticed. You will always know where they all are.

choices.text: Teach them what to look for

effects.log: You have it put about how a person can tell. It is very unpleasant information. Everyone in the house has started to look at each other's fingernails.

events.text: There are people out there who have been meeting about you, in back rooms, for some time now. It has occurred to them that you have left them a door. One of them has been to see {ot_child}, with a very sad face, to say how much {ot_he} is undervalued. {ot_He} did not throw them out. {ot_He} did not do anything else, either. You only know about it because {ot_foe} has mentioned it to you, in passing, so very casually.

choices.text: Ask {ot_child} about it directly

effects.log: {ot_He} tells you about it, and {ot_he} has an explanation. It is quite a good one. You are going to remember how long {ot_he} took before answering.

choices.text: Let the door stay open, and watch who comes through

effects.log: You have it watched. It is the best view you have had of them yet. It is also your own child they are standing next to, and you are the one who is watching.

events.text: Whoever it is that has been working against you has grown very fond of the question of who comes after. Rumours are being paid for. {ot_foe} is being told that you mean to pass {ot_fhim} over, and {ot_child} is being told the same thing about {ot_him}. If they could only be got to talk to each other about it, the whole thing would fall apart in an afternoon. They have not spoken to each other in three years.

choices.text: Lock them in a room together for an afternoon

effects.log: It is not the sort of thing a head of a great house usually does. There is shouting, and later there is rather less of it. They come out having agreed on one thing, and it is you.

choices.text: Use it. Let the rumours do your work

effects.log: It keeps them both very attentive. Your enemies are doing a good deal of your job for you, and you do not stop to think about what they are being paid in.

events.text: {ot_child} has come back to the morning business. Nobody asked {ot_him} to. It has been a long time since the afternoon you broke {ot_him}, and {ot_he} is older, and {ot_he} stands in the same place {ot_he} used to, and there is more grey in {ot_his} hair than there should be. A few people have started to stand near {ot_him} again. {ot_He} bows to you exactly as low as the form requires.

choices.text: Bow back, a little

effects.log: It is very slight. The whole hall has seen it. Nobody knows what it means, including you.

choices.text: Ask {ot_him} what {ot_he} wants

effects.log: {ot_He} says, in a very reasonable voice, that {ot_he} only wants what anybody wants. {ot_He} goes back to {ot_his} place, and you find you have been holding your breath.

events.text: You had thought that was finished. {ot_child} has been keeping very quiet for years, on a small allowance, in a small house. People have started going to see {ot_him}, on their way to other places. They say that {ot_he} gives very good advice and asks for nothing. You have had the house watched. It seems that {ot_he} grows a very good sort of cabbage. {ot_He} has sent you one, with {ot_his} respects.

choices.text: Eat the cabbage

effects.log: You have it boiled, and you eat it, in front of your whole household. It is a very good cabbage. It has been a long time since anyone made you laugh.

choices.text: Have it tasted first

effects.log: It is fine. It was always going to be fine. {ot_He} will have heard that you had it tasted, and that is what {ot_he} sent it for.

events.text: You built this from nothing on a bare mountain, and you remember what each stone cost. {ot_child} and {ot_foe} grew up as if it had always been here. Each has a plan for what it should become, and both have come to explain it on the very spot where you slept in the rain that first winter. They begin by telling you how much they respect your early work.

choices.text: Take them both out to sleep on the mountain, in the rain

effects.log: You make them do it, all three of you, one night, at your age. In the morning nobody is speaking. You do not know if it did any good. You have not been so happy in a decade.

choices.text: Hear the better plan, and let it be known which one it was

effects.log: It is {ot_child}'s, and it is very good. It is not what you built. You have it copied out and you sign it.

events.text: The first disciple you ever took, with you since the founding, has asked for a word. When you started this, they say, you said it would never be like the sects you left. They have been looking at the yard lately, with its two groups, and would like to know which of those old sects it reminds you of.

choices.text: Say that you know which one

effects.log: You name it. You both laugh, not very happily. It is the first honest talk you have had about this with anyone, and it helps for about a season.

choices.text: Say that this is what a sect is

effects.log: They nod. They have been expecting that. They go back to the yard, and you are alone with what you built.

events.text: The branch lines have remembered their old rights. The dynasty's ledger has room for a great many claims, and the head of the cadet line has been through it with a very sharp pencil. With nobody named, he points out, the branches get a voice under the old form. He has been to see {ot_child} and {ot_foe}, and says they were both extremely attentive.

choices.text: Meet the branches in full council, and let them speak

effects.log: They speak for three days. You have kept them inside the room, and you have given them a taste of what they want. They will want more of it.

choices.text: Remind him who keeps the ledger

effects.log: He bows, and he goes on with his pencil. The Elders have heard about it. Some of them are pleased, and it is not the ones you would have hoped.

events.text: A very distant cousin has turned up with a genealogy, and a large number of friends. Nobody takes it seriously, naturally. It only says, in very beautiful script, that if the main line were to fall into dispute over the heirship, which of course it never would, the seat should revert to the line of the third son. Both {ot_child} and {ot_foe} have invited him to dinner, to find out how much he would want to go away.

choices.text: Pay him to go away yourself

effects.log: He goes, and it was cheap at the price. He has left copies. (-300 taels)

choices.text: Have him stay, and be seen at your table

effects.log: It concentrates the mind. {ot_child} and {ot_foe} look at each other over his head with something very nearly like alliance.

events.text: The Inner Palace has opinions. The consorts receive their relations rather more often, and the lamp oil is being divided by a scheme that took two eunuchs a month to devise. {ot_child}'s mother's family has a great many cousins, and would like them remembered in the next round of appointments. Loyalty, you are told, has become a very fluid thing.

choices.text: Hold a banquet for the whole Inner Palace, and watch

effects.log: You watch who has been told to sit where. It is better than any report. The food is very good, and nobody eats any of it.

choices.text: Move a few cousins out of the capital

effects.log: They go, with honours. The consorts are all perfectly charming to you for the rest of the year, and you have your food tasted twice.

events.text: The Generals send a joint memorial on the importance of a settled succession. The Civil Officials send another, with better prose, on the importance of not being hasty. The Inner Court sends nothing, and is very busy. Each has a candidate. It is a long time since all three powers of the court agreed on anything, and what they agree on is that you are growing old.

choices.text: Inspect the Northern Army in person, on horseback

effects.log: You stay in the saddle for six hours. It costs you a week in bed, in secret. The memorials have stopped for now.

choices.text: Have the three of them answer one another's memorials

effects.log: It keeps them busy. The prose is magnificent. Nobody has been governing anything for months.

events.text: The house of {ot_child}'s mother has taken a new interest in {ot_him}. A very old aunt has come up the black steps with her own bed and settled in. Gifts have arrived, and guards, who are very good. The other houses have noticed, and ask if you would care to receive their consort-candidates. {ot_child} has not asked for any of this.

choices.text: Send the aunt home, with every honour

effects.log: It takes her a month to pack. Her house is cooler to you now. {ot_child} is a little less safe, and owes a little less.

choices.text: Let the house do as it likes

effects.log: The guards stay. The whole mountain can see whose they are. {ot_He} is safer, and {ot_he} now belongs to somebody.

events.text: One of the four houses offers to stand behind {ot_child}, for a small thing: its own clerk at the Hall of Tallies, and its name in the marriage rolls for the next generation. The other three would not be pleased. All four have been on this mountain longer than the throne, and have been known to wait a very long time.

choices.text: Refuse them, and let them know why

effects.log: You tell them to their faces. It does not raise them in your favour, and it does not lower you in theirs. {ot_child} has lost a good deal by it, and may never know.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let {ot_child} take it

effects.log: {ot_He} takes it. Now you have a very strong heir, or a very strong house with an heir in its pocket. It may take some years to find out which.

events.text: {npc} is the new {ot_title}. {He} has been in {ot_hall} for a long time, and has very good manners. It has been a matter of days, and there have already been three visits and a very nice sword. {He} comes up to you to pay {his} respects, and you ask what {he} wants, and {he} says what {his} predecessor said: {ot_want}. You wonder how much {he} knows about how {his} predecessor went.

choices.text: Tell {him} how {his} predecessor went

effects.log: You tell {him} all of it. {He} listens without moving. {He} thanks you, and you think {he} is going to be careful, and that is all that anyone can be.

choices.text: Tell {him} you are glad to see {him}

effects.log: {He} is very glad to be seen. {He} goes back to {ot_hall}, where the gifts are piling up.

events.text: A post does not stay empty. {npc} of {ot_hall} is not who anyone would have picked, which is presumably why {he} has it: both sides could live with {him}, and both think they will own {him} by spring. {He} is very quiet, and {he} seems to have a good memory. On {his} first day {he} had the old lock changed. Somebody asked {him} why, and {he} said that {he} had always wanted to see what it looked like from the inside.

choices.text: Have {him} to dinner

effects.log: It is a very long dinner, with very little conversation. You like {him}, and you intend to keep an eye on {him}.

choices.text: Leave {him} alone

effects.log: You leave {him} alone. The new lock is a very good one.

events.text: A troupe of puppeteers has come through town with an old story from no land you can name: {ot_bk_dead}, who held {ot_bk_seat} and would never say who came after, and {ot_bk_who}, who won it. The children cheer at the fight. You find yourself standing at the back in the cold, with your food going cold too, watching a wooden figure refuse to speak. You have no idea why you cannot leave.

choices.text: Stay until the end, and give them some silver

effects.log: You stay. The puppet master looks at you for some time as he takes it. He says that some people always stay.

choices.text: Go home. It is only a puppet

effects.log: You go home, and you think about it for a day or two longer than you would have expected.

events.text: An old drunk in an inn is telling it, for wine. {ot_bk_who} took {ot_bk_seat}, he says, after {ot_bk_dead} died with their mouth shut. He has every detail wrong, and you know that he has. You could not say how you know. You correct him on one point, the colour of something, without thinking. He stops and looks at you, and the whole table looks at you, and you find you have nothing else to say.

choices.text: Buy him a drink, and ask him how it ends

effects.log: He tells you it ends the way that they all end. You sit there for quite a while after he has gone to sleep.

choices.text: Leave

effects.log: You leave. It rains the whole way. You keep trying to remember what the colour was, and how you knew it.

events.text: You have come across a very old book in a stall, with a chapter in it on the fall of a great house: a head who loved all of their heirs, or none of them, and never named one. {ot_bk_dead} is the name it gives. It says that it was {ot_bk_who} who won, and that it was not worth what it cost. There is a little note in the margin, in faded ink, in a hand a great deal like your own.

choices.text: Buy the book

effects.log: You pay what the stall-keeper asks, without bargaining. You read that chapter once, and you do not read it again, and you keep it.

choices.text: Put it back

effects.log: You put it back. When you walk past the stall the next day, it has been sold.

events.text: Children are playing a game in the street, with a chair and a stick. One of them is the old one, who has to sit and say nothing. The others are {ot_bk_who} and the rest, and they have to get the chair without being seen. They have no idea where it comes from. When you ask them, they say that it is just what the game is. A small one looks up at you and says that the one in the chair always loses. That is the rule.

choices.text: Ask if you can have a turn in the chair

effects.log: They find it very funny. You sit, and you say nothing, for as long as they can stand it. It is much harder than it looks.

choices.text: Give them each a sweet, and go on

effects.log: They take the sweets and go back to the game. You can hear it all the way to the end of the street.

events.text: {ot_child} has something to ask you, now that you are on {ot_his} side. It is only a small thing, a date, a key, a list of who was on duty. Nobody would ever know. It is certainly not against any rule that you can think of, not exactly. It is the first time that you have been asked, and you understand that there will be a next time, and that it will not be small. {ot_foe} has also been very friendly lately.

choices.text: Do it, and do it well

effects.log: It is done by evening. {ot_child} sends you a short note. You have gone a good way deeper than you had meant to.

choices.text: Find a reason why it cannot be done

effects.log: It is a very good reason. {ot_He} accepts it with a smile. You had better hope that your side wins without you.

events.text: It has been some time since you took {ot_child}'s side, and you have been doing rather well out of it. Your hall's budget has been renewed without a question, and you have been asked to more dinners. Now a young officer of yours has come to you in private. He does not like what {ot_child}'s people have been asking him to do. He has a family, and he trusts you. He has written it all down, and he hands it to you.

choices.text: Give it to {ot_child}

effects.log: You hand it over. You do not ask what happens to the young officer. It is the first time you have not asked.

choices.text: Burn it, and find him a post a long way off

effects.log: You see him off yourself. {ot_child} has noticed that a very useful young person has gone away, and {ot_he} looks at you with mild interest.

events.text: It is over, and {ot_child} has won, and everyone remembers where you sat. {ot_He} sends for you that same week. There is a promotion in it, and a good deal of money, and a seat that is rather closer to where things are decided. You are told that you have been a great friend. It is not until you are walking home that you find you have started to think about what it is that {ot_he} now knows about you.

choices.text: Take it, and be grateful

effects.log: You take it. You are grateful, and you say so, and you are seen to say so. It is an excellent post.

choices.text: Take it, and start writing some things down

effects.log: You start a small book. It may never be needed. {ot_He} will have started one too.

events.text: Your side has won. There is a very long banquet, and you are placed high up. A number of people who have not spoken to you for years have remembered how fond of you they have always been. {ot_foe} is not there. You did not expect that you would notice it. {ot_child} raises a cup to you across the hall, and you raise yours, and it is very good tea.

choices.text: Ask quietly what became of {ot_foe}

effects.log: Someone tells you. You nod, and you ask for a little more tea.

choices.text: Ask nothing

effects.log: You ask nothing. You have got rather good at that.

events.text: It went the other way. {ot_foe} has come out on top, and you know exactly what that means, because you were at that dinner. Nothing has been done to you. Your post is still your post, and your budget has been very politely cut. {ot_fHe} greeted you in the corridor this morning, by name, with a pleasant smile, and asked after your health. {ot_fHe} has a remarkable memory. Everyone has always said so.

choices.text: Go to {ot_foe} and offer your service, plainly

effects.log: {ot_fHe} accepts it, with that same smile. You are going to be working very hard for a very long time, and you will not be told what for.

choices.text: Keep your head down, and wait

effects.log: You keep it down. It is a long wait. You have begun to keep a bag packed.

events.text: {ot_child} has lost, and {ot_he} has been sent a long way off, and nobody is talking about {ot_him}. They are, however, talking about you, in the quiet way that they do. A number of invitations have failed to arrive. {ot_foe}'s people have been going through your old reports, and they have found them very interesting, and they have not yet told you what they plan to do about it. That seems to be the idea.

choices.text: Send {ot_child} a letter, wherever {ot_he} is

effects.log: You send it. It would have been wiser not to, and you know who is going to read it first. It is short, and it says what you meant.

choices.text: Burn everything with {ot_his} name on it

effects.log: It makes a very small fire, for all that it cost you. You stand and watch it for a while.

events.text: It is over, and you did not choose. {ot_foe} has won, or {ot_child} has, depending on who you ask this month. Neither of them has any reason to thank you. Neither of them has any reason to do anything about you, either. You are still at your post. There are not many left who can say so, and a good few people have started coming to you, quietly, to ask how you managed it.

choices.text: Tell them it was cowardice

effects.log: They all laugh. You let them. It was mostly cowardice, and it worked very well.

choices.text: Tell them nothing

effects.log: You give them some tea. There is a kind of respect in how they look at you now, and it is rather lonely.

events.text: You stayed out of it, and you have had a very peaceful few years. You are told that some very good people are gone now, on both sides, people you used to share a table with. There is a lot more room at the table. {ot_child} sends you a small gift at New Year, and so does {ot_foe}, as you might send something to a mountain that you had once considered going around.

choices.text: Send them both something back, of the same size

effects.log: You are very careful about the size. It is the only politics that you still do, and you have got very good at it.

choices.text: Send nothing

effects.log: You send nothing. They do not notice. That, you suppose, is what you were after.

events.text: There is a lull while both sides count. The roads are full of people carrying their beds from one place to another. A very frightened delegation of common people has brought you a sack of rice and a simple request. They would like to know when it will be over, and which of you they are supposed to be afraid of. {ot_foe} has told them what you are about to.

choices.text: Open your stores to them

effects.log: It costs you an army's rations. They carry the news home, down roads that {ot_foe} also has to use.

choices.text: Tell them that it will be over soon

effects.log: You tell them. They bow, and leave the rice. You have it sent to your soldiers, and the soldiers eat it.

events.text: Someone has come over to you in the night, from {ot_foe}'s side. They are one of those who knew you both when you were small, and they look very old. They do not ask for anything. They say {ot_foe} has not been sleeping, and that sometimes {ot_fhe} asks about you. They have also brought you, for what it may be worth, the plan for the next three months. You hold it in your hand for a while.

choices.text: Use it

effects.log: It is a very good plan, and now it is no good to anybody. {ot_foe} loses a great many people that month. You do not sleep either.

choices.text: Send it back, with the old servant

effects.log: You send them back with a safe conduct. It costs you the plan. There are some people on both sides who will remember that this was done.

events.text: The great houses of the murim send condolences on the death, and on the state of your affairs. Several would be glad to help, for some small consideration on the border, in the treasury, or in the matter of a marriage. {ot_foe} has had the same letters. You can tell by the stationery.

choices.text: Refuse them all, and say it is a family matter

effects.log: You send a very short letter. It wins you nothing but some respect, from the sort of people who cannot help you. Your people have heard about it, however.

choices.text: Take the help, and sign what they want

effects.log: You sign. Their people arrive within the month, in good order. You have a much better chance now of winning something, and rather less of it to win.

events.text: You are getting old, or you are getting tired, and neither of them is going to stop on that account. {ot_child} has started bringing you your medicine, personally. {ot_foe} has started bringing you the news. Each of them is extremely attentive, and you have never been so well looked after in your life. You had a dream that you woke up and had already said it, and everyone had gone home.

choices.text: Say something to them, at last

effects.log: You start to, at dinner. You see them both stop eating. You ask for the salt.

choices.text: Take the medicine and read the news

effects.log: They are both very good. You are looked after beautifully. It goes on.

events.text: It has gone on longer than some wars. There are young people in the house who cannot remember a time without two sides, and have married into it. You hear a little girl ask which side the cook is on, and she gets a very sensible answer. {ot_child} and {ot_foe} are grey at the temples now, and you still think of them as children.

choices.text: Look at them properly, for once

effects.log: You look. They have got old, and you have missed it. You do not know what to do about that, so you have some tea sent over.

choices.text: Get back to work

effects.log: There is plenty to do. There always is, and that has been the trouble.
